# Salutations to the Illustrious Ganesha. Salutations to the Illustrious Lord of Venkata. Now begins the *Sarvartha Chintamani* <note>The "Gemstone of All Desired Meanings," a classic 13th-century Sanskrit treatise on predictive astrology.</note>.

->Salutations to the Guru, Lord Venkatesha, who resides upon the banks of the magnificent Shesha Hill <note>Tirumala</note>. I, the wise son of Arya, having bowed daily to the Lord of Venkata, shall now compose the *Sarvartha Chintamani*—a vessel for crossing the great ocean of the science of light <term>Jyotish: the traditional Indian system of astronomy and astrology</term>—for the benefit of those learned in the ripening of astrological wisdom. (1)<-

->I bow to the elephant-faced Ganesha, who possesses the luster of a blue lotus, who fulfills desires in an instant, and before whom all the gods prostrate. (2)<-

->May the Goddess <note>Saraswati</note>, the bestower of the wealth of speech, who sits upon a white lotus and whose form is as white as cow’s milk, reside upon my tongue. (3)<-

->May all the zodiac signs beginning with Aries, and the planets led by the Sun, who act for the benefit of the world, protect me here always. (4)<-

Whatever has been declared in the birth charts <term>Jataka: natal astrology</term> of humans on earth, the experts say all of that applies to horary questions <term>Prashna: the branch of astrology answering specific questions based on the time they are asked</term> as well. A question is similar to a birth; there is no difference between a question and a birth in this system. (5)

Mars, Venus, Mercury, the Moon, the Sun, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Saturn, and Jupiter are the lords of the signs beginning with Aries in order; they are also the lords of the subdivisions <term>Amshas: divisional portions of a zodiac sign</term> of those signs. (6)

The signs from Aries onward represent the head, face, throat, chest, heart, stomach, waist, bladder, private parts, thighs, the two knees, shanks, and feet. Whichever part is associated with a malefic planet <note>planets considered naturally unfavorable, such as Mars or Saturn</note> suffers affliction. (7)

Two fish joined tail-to-head <note>Pisces</note>, a man with the legs of a horse and a bow <note>Sagittarius</note>, a human pair—one holding a staff and the other a lute <note>Gemini</note>, a woman in a boat holding fire and grain <note>Virgo</note>, and a merchant holding scales <note>Libra</note>...

...and || 8 || One who desires to grasp the water-clock <note>original: "ghati-jala"; a traditional device for measuring time</note> should know that the remaining signs are consistent with their names. Aries is indeed Aries, Taurus is the same, Cancer is the Crab <note>original: "Kulira"</note>, and Scorpio is the Scorpion <note>original: "Ali"</note>. || 9 ||

By dividing a sign into three parts, they call it a **Drekkana** <note>a decan or 10-degree division</note>. The lords of these are the lords of the sign itself, the lord of the 5th house from it, and the lord of the 9th house from it. In an even sign, the Moon and Sun are the lords of the two halves of the house; in an odd sign, the Sun and Moon are the lords of the halves <note>This refers to the **Hora** division of 15 degrees each</note>. || 10 ||

In moveable signs, the lords of the **Navamshas** <note>ninth-parts, 3°20' each</note> begin from the lord of that sign; in fixed signs, they begin from the lord of the ninth sign from it; in dual signs, they begin from the lord of the fifth sign from it. So say the great experts in the meaning of the Shastras <note>sacred scientific texts</note>. || 11 ||

The lords of the **Dwadasamshas** <note>twelfth-parts, 2°30' each</note> begin from the lord of that specific field <note>the sign itself</note>. The lords of the divisions of the Ascendant are determined by their respective rulers. The lords of the **Trimshamshas** <note>degree-divisions of unequal length used for strength and character</note> are Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, Mercury, and Venus in an odd sign. In an even sign, || 12 ||

it is the reverse. The degrees are assigned in groups of five, five, eight, seven, and five <note>original: "pancha-shara-ashta-sapta-bana"</note> as stated in many scriptures. The lords of the **Saptamshas** <note>seventh-parts</note> in an odd sign start from the lord of that sign; in an even sign, they start from the lord of the seventh sign from it. || 13 ||

The lords of the **Dashamshas** <note>tenth-parts</note> in an odd sign start from the lord of that sign; in an even sign, they start from the lord of the ninth sign from it. In an odd sign, the lords of the **Kalamsas** <note>sixteenth-parts, also called Shodashamsha</note> are Brahma <note>the Creator</note>, Vishnu <note>the Preserver</note>, Shiva <note>the Destroyer</note>, and the Sun. || 14 ||

In an even sign, the order is reversed. In an odd sign, the lords of the **Shashtyamsas** <note>sixtieth-parts, 0°30' each</note> are: 1. Ghora <note>Terrible</note>, 2. <term>Drekkana</term>: A 10-degree division of a zodiac sign, used to refine astrological predictions.
<term>Trimshamsha</term>: A division of a sign into 30 parts, though often grouped into five unequal sections ruled by the non-luminary planets.
<term>Shashtyamsa</term>: A minute division of 30 arc-minutes (1/60th of a sign), each associated with a specific deity or quality that colors the planet's influence.

...so it shall be. || 26 || The ninth <term>Vaisheshikamsha</term> <note>A specific system of measuring planetary strength based on how many favorable divisions a planet occupies</note> is called Airavata. Now, the individual fruits of these positions are described. When considering the combination of the ten-fold divisions <note>original: "Dashavarga"</note>, the learned recognize the "Distinguished Divisions" <note>original: "Vaisheshikamshaka"</note>. || 27 || One born with a planet in the **Airavata** division becomes a universal monarch <note>original: "Sarvabhauma"</note> endowed with all forms of lordship and wealth. In the **Devaloka** division, one becomes a king, a lord of the earth, and a great performer of charity. || 28 || In the **Paravata** division, one becomes a regional ruler <note>original: "Mandalika"</note> and an expert in all classical sciences. In the **Parijata** division, one is possessed of great riches. || 30 || In the **Svansha** <note>The planet's own division</note> position, one becomes famous, intelligent, and endowed with every happiness. || 31 ||

### Now, the Temporary Planetary States

The experts declare that the <term>Lagna</term> <note>The Ascendant or rising sign</note> lasts for a duration of two and a half <term>Ghatis</term> <note>A traditional unit of time equal to 24 minutes; 2.5 Ghatis equals one hour</note> sequentially for the signs starting from Aries. The <term>Pranapada</term> <note>A sensitive point in a horoscope related to life-force</note> is calculated as one-fourth of a Ghati starting from the lord of the sign. || 1 || For the Sun, the calculation reverses from Sagittarius for two and a half Ghatis; for the Moon, it is also from that point. For Mars, the time is two and a half Ghatis sequentially, but from Taurus, it is just one Ghati in reverse. || 2 || For Mercury, it is one Ghati in reverse from Sagittarius. For Jupiter, it is five Ghatis downward from Pisces. For Venus, the duration is one Ghati starting from Gemini. For Saturn, the son of the Day-Lord... || 3 || ...following the reverse path, the duration is one Ghati. For Jupiter, it is two and a half Ghatis from Aries. For Ketu <note>original: "Shikhi"</note>, it is the same from Pisces in reverse order. The noble teachers have described the results of these in other scriptures. || 4 ||

The states of the planets, such as "Infancy" and so on, are said to be sequential in odd signs and reversed in even signs. The states are: **Infant**, **Youth**, **Adult**, **Old**, and **Dead**, determined by the progression of the <term>Amshas</term> <note>Degrees/divisions</note> in groups of six. ||

### The Names of the Zodiac Signs

The first sign is **Aries**, also known as *Aja* <note>original: "aja" - goat</note>, *Vasta*, and *Kriya*. The second is **Taurus**, called *Uksha* and *Go*, which is the abode of Venus. || 6 || The third is the sign of Mercury, **Gemini**, known as *Nriyugma* <note>original: "nriyugma" - human pair</note> and *Jituma*. The fourth sign is **Cancer**, belonging to the Moon and called *Kulira*. The fifth is **Leo**, with the names *Kanthirava* and *Leya*. The sixth is **Virgo**, called *Pathona*, *Abala* <note>original: "abala" - woman/weak one</note>, and *Tanvi*. || 7 ||

The seventh is **Libra**, known as *Juka*, *Vanik* <note>original: "vanik" - merchant</note>, and *Tauli*. The eighth is **Scorpio**, the abode of Mars, known as *Kaurpya* and *Ali*. The ninth is **Sagittarius**, the sign of Jupiter, called *Taukshika* and *Chapa* <note>original: "chapa" - bow</note>. The tenth is **Capricorn**, known as *Akekara* and *Chakra*. || 8 || The eleventh is **Aquarius**, known as *Hridroga* and *Kumbha* <note>original: "kumbha" - water pot</note>. The final sign is **Pisces**, called *Jhasha* and *Riphantya*.

### The Significance of the Twelve Houses

The **First House** <term>Hora: the Ascendant or rising sign</term> represents the body, death, birth, and the head. The **Second House** represents speech, wealth, family, and the eyes. || 9 || The **Third House** is known as the place of siblings, the throat, valor, and the ears. The **Fourth House** signifies happiness, water, kinsmen, the underworld <note>original: "patala"</note>, the heart, vehicles, and the mother. || 10 ||

The **Fifth House** is the place of intellect, influence, children, and sacred mantras; it represents the power of discernment and the stomach region. || 11 || The **Sixth House** represents disease, wounds, enemies, vices, and thieves. The **Seventh House** is the place of desire, the spouse, and partnerships. || 12 ||

The **Eighth House** relates to fluids, molasses, urinary difficulties, the private parts, and the span of life or death. The **Ninth House** is the place of righteousness <term>Dharma: religious merit and duty</term>, fortune, the father, the teacher, and penance. || 12 || The **Tenth House** represents authority, honor, profession, and the sky. The **Eleventh House** is the place of gains and income. The **Twelfth House** is the place of expenditure and loss; the great sages say this concludes the divisions from the Ascendant. || 13 ||

### Characteristics of the Signs

The sixth, eighth, and twelfth houses are known as the "difficult houses" <note>original: "dusthana"</note> as they are sources of destruction. Taurus, Aries, Sagittarius, Cancer, and Capricorn rise from the rear <note>original: "prishtodaya" - back-rising signs</note> and are strong during the night. The remaining signs are strong during the day and rise from the head <note>original: "shirshodaya" - head-rising signs</note>, while Pisces rises...

The son of the Moon <note>Mercury</note> is the Prince. Venus and Jupiter are the Ministers. Saturn is the Servant; one born under his influence takes up such a profession. || 23 || The Sun is the Soul; the Moon is the Mind; Mars is Strength; Mercury is Speech; Jupiter is Knowledge and Happiness; Venus is Desire; and the son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note> is Sorrow. || 24 ||

The Sun is called *Heli*, *Bhanuman* <note>The Possessor of Rays</note>, *Diptarashmi* <note>He of Radiant Beams</note>, *Chandanshu* <note>Hot-Rayed One</note>, *Bhaskara* <note>The Light-Maker</note>, and *Ahaskara* <note>The Day-Maker</note>. The Moon is *Abja* <note>Born of the Waters</note>, *Soma*, *Chandramas*, *Shitarashmi* <note>Cool-Rayed One</note>, *Shitanshu*, *Glau*, *Mriganka* <note>The Deer-Marked One</note>, and *Kalaisha* <note>Lord of the Phases</note>. || 25 ||

*Ara*, *Vakra* <note>The Twisted/Crooked</note>, *Avaneya* <note>Son of the Earth</note>, *Kuja*, *Bhauma*, *Krura* <note>The Cruel</note>, *Lohitanga* <note>The Red-Bodied</note>, and the Sinner <note>the Malefic</note> are names for Mars. *Vid*, *Jna*, *Saumya*, *Bodhana*, *Chandraputra* <note>Son of the Moon</note>, *Chandri*, the Peaceful One, the Dark-Bodied, and the Very Tall are names for Mercury. || 26 ||

The Son of the Shadow, the Lame One, *Yama*, the Son of the Sun, *Kona*, the Dark One, the Son of Shani, and the Blue One are names for Saturn. He is cruel, thin-bodied, with yellowish eyes, and tall. *Tamas* <note>Darkness</note>, *Asura*, *Agu*, and *Saimhikeya* <note>Son of Simhika</note> || 28 ||

*Svarbhanu*, *Rahu*, and the Devourer of the Moon are names for the North Node. *Ketu*, *Shikhi*, and names meaning "Banner" are for the South Node. The son of Saturn is *Gulika* or *Mandi*, the son of Yama, the Taker of Life, and a great sinner <note>highly malefic</note>. || 29 ||

*Prana* <note>Life-force</note> is the name for the *Pranapada* <note>a sensitive mathematical point in a horoscope</note>; those who know say these are synonyms. The Sun has a body marked by the limbs of the Ages <note>Yugas</note>, is red and dark-hued, and has the luster of tawny eyes. || 30 ||

He <note>the Sun</note> is of a bilious <term>Pitta: the fire and water element in Ayurvedic medicine</term> nature, has a symmetrical body, is full of majesty, possesses the quality of Goodness <term>Sattva: the quality of purity and light</term>, and has little hair. He is fond of wandering, speaks in concise sentences, gives sparingly, and possesses divine intelligence. || 31 ||

The Moon is white-bodied, has a symmetrical frame, is eloquent, and possesses a discerning mind. Sometimes thin <note>waning</note>, he is of a cool nature—

For Saturn <note>original: "Saurasya"</note>, the friends are Venus <note>original: "Bhriguputra"</note> and Mercury <note>original: "Saumya"</note>; Jupiter <note>original: "Guru"</note> is neutral, and all others are enemies. For Rahu <note>the North Node</note>, the friends are Venus, Jupiter, and Saturn; the experts say the same applies to Ketu <note>the South Node</note> in this system. || 60 ||

All planets become "temporal friends" <note>original: "Tatkalika Mitra"</note> when they are positioned in the second, third, fourth, tenth, eleventh, and twelfth houses from one another. If they are situated in other houses, they become "temporal enemies" for that specific time. || 61 ||

When a planet is both a natural friend <note>original: "Nisarga Mitra"</note> and a temporal friend, it is designated a "Great Friend" <term>Adhimitra: a planet that provides exceptionally positive results due to double friendship</term>. Likewise, if it is an enemy in both ways, it is a "Great Enemy" <term>Adhishatru</term>. If it is a friend in one way and an enemy in the other, it becomes "Neutral." || 62 ||

A lord of the planets attains "Positional Strength" <term>Sthana Bala: strength derived from a planet's zodiacal location</term> when it is in its sign of exaltation, in a friend's sign, in its own <term>Navamsha: a 1/9th divisional chart</term>, in its own sign, in its own <term>Drekkana: a 1/10th divisional chart</term>, or in its own <term>Dvadasamsha: a 1/12th divisional chart</term>. || 63 ||

Mercury and Jupiter are powerful in the East <note>the 1st House/Ascendant</note>. The Sun and Mars possess strength in the South <note>the 10th House</note>. Saturn is powerful in the West <note>the 7th House</note>. The Moon and Venus are powerful in the North <note>the 4th House</note>. || 64 ||

In the seventh house from these positions, they are said to be devoid of "Directional Strength" <term>Dig Bala</term>; for positions in between, the strength should be calculated by proportion. The Sun and other planets are also endowed with strength during their own months, <term>Horas: planetary hours</term>, days, and years. || 65 ||

Saturn, the Moon, and Mars are powerful at night. The Sun, Jupiter, and Venus are powerful during the day. Mercury is always powerful. During the bright fortnight <note>waxing moon</note>, the benefic planets are strong, and during the dark fortnight <note>waning moon</note>, the others <note>malefics</note> are strong in sequence. || 66 ||

Planets are at full strength when aspected by benefics and not aspected by malefic planets. The Sun is exceedingly powerful during its Northern Course <term>Uttarayana: the period between the winter and summer solstices</term>, while the Moon is full of strength at other times. || 67 ||

Mars and the other planets <note>excluding the Sun and Moon</note> are powerful when in retrograde motion. A planet is also victorious in "planetary war" <note>when two planets are in close conjunction</note> if it possesses brilliance and is situated in the North. In terms of "Natural Strength" <term>Naisargika Bala</term>, the planets are stronger in this increasing order: Saturn, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Moon, and Sun. || 68 ||

The strength of the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note> is dependent on the strength of its Lord...

# Chapter 1

-> Indeed, all the masters declare the **Sixfold Strength** <term>Shadvidha Virya: the six primary sources of planetary power in Indian astrology: Positional, Directional, Temporal, Motional, Aspectual, and Natural strength</term> in this manner. If the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term> is a human sign, its strength is one full unit <note>original: "rupa", a standard unit of measure in astrological calculation</note>. If it is a four-footed sign, it is considered half-strength. If the Ascendant is a creature sign <note>specifically Scorpio, the scorpion</note>, it is said to have no clear strength at all. <-

### 69. 6.30 <note>6 units and 30 minutes of arc</note>

The Sun is most powerful; the Moon’s strength is six; Mars <note>original: "Vasundhara-raja", King of the Earth</note> is five. Mercury <note>original: "Indu-suna", Son of the Moon</note> is six and a half; Jupiter is five and a half.

### 70. 6.30

Then Venus is powerful at seven. Saturn is five. This is the combination of the six strengths; otherwise, they would be different. For the Sun, they desire three units of strength; then for Directional strength <term>Dig-bala: strength gained by being in a specific cardinal direction</term>, it is two and three-quarters.

### 71. 2.45 / 0.45

For Positional strength, it is one unit minus a quarter. For Motional strength <term>Cheshta-bala: strength derived from the planet's specific movement or speed</term>, it is one unit minus a sixth part. For Temporal strength <term>Kala-virya: strength derived from the time of day, month, or year</term>, it is two units minus an eighth part.

### 72. 0.50 / 3.30 / 0.30

The full strengths of the Sun, Moon, Mercury, and Jupiter are given; however, the strength born of the Solstice <term>Ayanaja-bala: strength related to the planet's declination north or south of the equator</term> is half a unit when calculated separately. For the Moon, they say Directional strength is one unit minus a sixth.

### 73. 0.50 / 2.15 / 1.40 / 30

For Positional strength, it is two units plus a quarter. For Temporal strength, it is two units minus a third. For Motional strength, it is exactly half a unit. For the Moon, Venus, and Jupiter, the Solstitial strength is one unit minus a third.

### 74. 0.40 / 0.40 / 1.7.30

For these same planets, the Motional strength is one unit minus a third. The Temporal strength is one unit plus one-eighth and thirty seconds. For Saturn and Mars <note>original: "Dinesha-putra" (Son of the Sun) and "Vasundhara-suna" (Son of the Earth)</note>, the Directional strength is half a unit.

### 75. 0.30 / 0.20 / 2.30

The Solstitial strength is one-third of a unit. The Positional strength is two and a half units. These strengths are declared in sequence for the Son of the Sun and the Son of the Earth. These strengths increase until they reach the midpoint of the astrological house <term>Bhava: the twelve divisions of the sky relative to the observer</term>, and from there, they decrease. When a planet is in its sign of exaltation or a friend's sign, it attains its primary strength through these six divisions.

One should then calculate the precise position here, just as one does for the Ascendant. || 95 || From the <term>Pakesha</term><note>The lord of the planetary period or Dasha currently in operation</note>, if the lord of the sub-period is situated in the 8th, 6th, or 12th house from it, he becomes an enemy. If he is in the 11th, 2nd, 3rd, 5th, 9th, or 10th house, and associated with a planet, he is called "Very Auspicious." However, a planet associated with the 7th house from him is said to give inauspicious results; this is the established order of the planets. || 96 || A celestial body associated with malefic planets becomes an enemy; yet, depending on its placement, even a malefic can be called "Very Auspicious" if it grants good results. The sages, having reflected upon the results according to position and knowing the path of the planets, speak for the ultimate success of the worlds. || 97 || This Chapter on Definitions has been described, extracting the essence from all the sciences for the benefit of all people. Whatever Venkatesha has understood, he should apply all of that to the planetary periods and their results. || 98 ||

### Thus ends the First Chapter of the Sarvartha Chintamani.

->Adoration to Lord Ganesha<-

Since various appropriate results arise from the houses, and because the intellects of others are bound by the technicalities of different treatises, I shall describe those very results arising from planetary combinations. Having examined them with my intellect, I do this for the delight of the learned. || 1 || All houses associated with or aspected by auspicious lords or natural benefics grant their full results, provided they are free from the sight or association of malefic planets. Even if all the lords of the houses are malefics, they are said to grant auspicious results if the planets are not in debilitation, combustion, or in an enemy's sign. || 2 || If malefic planets or the lords of those houses are in the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses <note>original: "ripu-randhra-ripha"</note> from the Ascendant or any other house, they do not grant full results. The wise speak of the results of the houses in this manner. || 3 || Whichever house lord is in the 6th, 8th, or 12th, or if the lord of a "bad house" <note>dusthana</note> is situated in a particular house...

Those who know the science <note>astrologers</note> say that the destruction of a house's significance occurs when it is not aspected by benefics; however, if the house is aspected by auspicious planets, it brings happiness. || 4 || If the 1st, 5th, 9th <note>the trines</note>, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses are occupied by benefic planets, are free from the sight of malefic planets, and are joined by the lord of that house without any malefic influence, then the sages declare the full prosperity and auspiciousness of those houses. If the opposite conditions exist, destruction occurs. If there is a mixture of influences, the results for the body <note>1st house</note> and other houses will be mixed. || 5 ||

If the lord of a house is placed in a house of destruction <note>the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses</note>, or is combust <note>rendered invisible</note> by the rays of the Sun, or is in a debilitated or inimical sign, and is neither joined nor aspected by benefics, the sages declare the total destruction of that house's significance. Even if planets occupy that house, they will not yield fruit in such a state. This applies to the body and all other houses in order. || 6 ||

One should predict the acquisition of wealth based on the strength of the Ascendant and the Moon. Wealth may come from the father, mother, enemies, friends, or brothers through the planets situated in the 10th house <note>the house of profession</note>. Or it may come from servants. Among the Sun, the Ascendant, and the Moon, whoever is strongest determines the source. Those learned in this science say that one's livelihood is determined by the lord of the Navamsha <note>a 1/9th divisional chart</note> in which the lord of the 10th house is placed. || 7 ||

If that Navamsha lord is the Sun, the person lives by medicine, gold, liquids, trade, pearls, or perhaps by deceiving others. They might also work as a messenger or a traveler. || 8 || <note>Note: Verse 8 and 9 both mention the Sun's portion, likely referring to different planetary strengths or variations in the tradition.</note>

Through the teaching of sacred chants <term>Mantras</term>, the practice of alchemy <term>Rasavada</term>, or through entertainment and the study of all scriptures and ancient histories <term>Puranas</term>, or by the path of spiritual instruction, one becomes honored by kings and makes a living, if the Sun is the lord of that portion. || 9 ||

Through the buying and selling of water-born products, through wells, or the playing of the drum <term>Mridanga</term> and other musical instruments; or through the patronage of royal women, or the sale of clothes, one earns a living if the Sun <note>or Moon, depending on the specific commentary tradition</note> rules the portion. || 10 ||

Through disputes over metals, through wounds received in battle, through the manipulation of fire, or through engaging in quarrels, one lives by the path of courage or even through the life of a thief, if the son of the Earth <note>Mars</note> rules the portion. || 11 || Through crafts, arts, or poetry—

Through the knowledge of the science of the stars <note>original: "Jyotir-gana-jnana"; referring to astronomy and astrology</note>, if the planet is in the subdivision of Mercury <note>original: "Buddhansha"</note>, one gains a livelihood through the path of the sacred scriptures <note>original: "Agama-shastra"</note>. One may also find success through the study of the Vedas for the sake of wealth, through the chanting of prayers, or by acting as a family priest. **12**

In the subdivision of Jupiter <note>original: "Jivansha"</note>, the livelihood comes from the path of worshiping the gods and the twice-born <note>original: "Bhusura"; referring to Brahmins</note>, or through teaching. It is said that wealth comes from the Puranas, the law books <note>original: "Shastra"</note>, the path of moral conduct, religious instruction, or through lending money <note>original: "Kusida"; banking or usury</note>. **13**

The ancient teachers say that life's sustenance comes from gold, rubies, elephants, horses, and the purchase of land. If the planet is in the subdivision of Venus <note>original: "Bhrigoh-sutanshu"</note>, one gains through the sale of molasses, cooked rice, milk, and curd, or through the attraction of women. **14**

In the subdivision of Saturn <note>original: "Shanyansha"</note>, one lives by base or despised paths, through crafts, working with wood, or through acts of violence. It may also come from carrying heavy loads, deceiving people, or through the root causes of mutual enmity and conflict. **15**

->**The Strength of the Planets**<-

When a planet is in its own sign, its own ninth-part subdivision <note>term: Navamsha; a 3.20 degree division used to determine a planet's hidden strength</note>, in a friend's sign, or in its highest exaltation; or when it is in its own decan <note>term: Dreshkana; a 10 degree division of a sign</note>, in the four cardinal houses, or in its primary triangle <note>original: "Mula-trikona"; a specific favorable position for a planet</note>; or if the planets are endowed with temporal strength or are in the best subdivision <note>original: "Vargottama"; when a planet is in the same sign in both the main chart and the ninth-part chart</note>—then all these planets truly grant auspicious results during their major and minor periods <note>term: Dasha/Antardasha; the system of planetary timing in Indian astrology</note>. **16**

The lord of the eighth house <note>original: "Randhrapa"; the house of death and transformation</note>, or the lord of the twenty-second decan <note>original: "Kharesha"; a sensitive point in the horoscope associated with danger</note>, or the son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note>, or the lord of the point of doom <note>original: "Maandhisha"; referring to the mathematical point Gulika/Maandi</note>, or the lord of the ninth-part subdivision of these—whichever among these planets is of a cruel nature, **17** or is the great enemy of the lord of a particular house, or is a planet occupying a sign with no strength points <note>original: "Bindu-shunya"; referring to the Ashtakavarga system of point-based strength</note>—the astrologer and the questioner should declare the destruction of the body, wealth, and other matters during the ripening <note>original: "Paka"; the period when a planet's results manifest</note> of those planets. **18**

Saturn, the point of doom, the lord of the twenty-second decan, the lord of the eighth house, and the lords of their ninth-part subdivisions—the weak periods of these planets grant death when the son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note> travels through a difficult sign. **19**

If the lord of the house of wealth is a malefic planet, then during the minor periods of Saturn, Mars, Rahu <note>original: "Bhogi"; the North Node of the Moon</note>, or the Sun, they say wealth will be destroyed. The same occurs if malefic planets are present in that house. **20**

From the wrath of the protector of the earth <note>original: "kshitipala"; refers to the King or government</note>, one should predict the destruction of various types of wealth for men, as well as displacement from one's position and opposition from one's own beloved people. || 21 || During the sub-period <note>original: "apahara-kale"</note> of malefic planets, or during the major periods <note>original: "dashasu"</note> of a malefic planet itself, wealth, honor, children, and siblings come to ruin; however, if influenced by benefics, these faults do not occur. || 22 || When a beautiful celestial body <note>a benefic planet</note> is the lord of the house of wealth, one attains the gain of wealth during its ripening period <note>the planetary period</note>. Confusion of the intellect and the consumption of bad food occur during the period of the lord of the house of children <note>the 5th house</note> if it is a malefic planet. Those who have mastered the various scriptures state that a four-footed <term>quadruped: chatuṣpada</term> is born when the rising sign is of a non-human species <note>original: "viyonī", referring to animal or non-human births</note>. || 51 || If a bird-shaped <term>decan: dṛkāṇa</term> <note>A 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</note> is rising and is aspected by a powerful planet, or if the rising sign is a moveable sign, or if the <term>nine-fold division: navāṃśa</term> belongs to Mercury, a non-human birth occurs. || 52 ||

If the rising sign is aspected by Venus, a cow is born; if by Saturn, a buffalo. If the rising sign is associated with or aspected by Rahu <note>the North Node of the Moon</note> or Ketu <note>the South Node</note>, a goat or sheep is born; and by other planets, other types of animals are produced. || 53 ||

When the lord of the 6th house is in a sign owned by Mercury in the ascendant, and the lord of the ascendant is also in a sign of Mercury, the person born will be a <term>hermaphrodite: napuṃsaka</term> possessing female characteristics. Through the combination of Saturn and Mars, a male eunuch is born. || 54 ||

If the Moon and the Sun aspect each other, or if Mercury and Saturn are in even and odd signs respectively; or if Saturn in an odd sign aspects the Sun in an even sign; || 55 || or if the Moon is in an odd ascendant and is aspected by Mars in an even sign; or if Mercury and the Moon are in even and odd signs and are aspected by Mars from the ascendant or from the Moon; || 56 || these are the six "neuter combinations" <note>original: "klībayogāḥ"</note> described by the great sages learned in many scriptures. Furthermore, if the lord of the ascendant is joined with Mercury and is not aspected by any benefic planets, one becomes a eunuch. || 57 ||

If the lords of the 10th and 9th houses are in "bad houses" <note>the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses</note> while the lord of the ascendant is strong, the person is born without the performance of the <term>parting of the hair: sīmantakarma</term> <note>A traditional Hindu prenatal rite of passage performed for the mother's well-being</note>; such a person is considered "primary" or base in that regard. || 58 ||

If a malefic planet is in the 11th house or if the lord of that house is malefic, the person is likewise considered base. If Leo is rising, the house has two doors; if Virgo is rising, even with a planet in its "fall" <note>original: "nīcagraha", a planet in its weakest zodiacal position</note>, the birth is as described. || 59 ||

The direction of the door of the birth-chamber is said to be indicated by the lord of the <term>nine-fold division: navāṃśa</term> or by the sign and decan of the ascendant. Alternatively, the door is indicated by the lord of the ascendant or by powerful planets situated in the <term>cardinal houses: kendra</term>. || 60 ||

# Chapter 2

The attendants present at the time of birth should be determined by the planets. If Saturn is situated there, the attendant is a woman of the laborer class <note>original: "shudra"</note>; if the Sun is situated there, she is a woman of the warrior class <note>original: "kshatriya"</note>. || 61 ||

If Rahu or Ketu <note>The North and South nodes of the Moon, often called the "shadow planets"</note> are present, she is from an outcaste group; with other planets, she is said to be of a class equal to the family. The attendants present at that time are also indicated by the planets occupying the second, twelfth, and fourth houses. || 62 ||

Some authorities say this should be determined by the lords of those houses or the planets associated with them. If Jupiter, Mercury, or Venus <note>original: "suradevapujyaih" - those worshiped by the gods</note> are situated there, the attendant is a beautiful woman of the priestly class <note>original: "brahmakula"</note>. || 63 ||

If these planets are associated with cruel or malefic divisions <note>term: papamshaka - a sub-division of a zodiac sign ruled by a malefic planet</note>, those women are said to be widows. If they are joined with Rahu or Ketu, the women are of ill-repute; if joined with Saturn, || 64 ||

she will be dark-complexioned, hunchbacked, or a widow. One should state the number of attendants based on the combination of planets. By the planets situated in the visible half of the zodiac, one determines if they are outside or inside the house. || 65 ||

One should state the number based on those planets; if many are in a single sign, they say there are many attendants. They describe the flickering of the lamp if the sign is "movable" <note>term: chara - signs like Aries or Cancer that represent change</note>; if the sign is "fixed," the flame is steady at that time. || 66 ||

In a dual-natured sign <note>original: "videharashau"</note>, the lamp is held in the hand. The quantity of oil is told by the Moon, and the wick is determined by the Ascendant <note>term: Lagna - the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note>, according to some. || 67 ||

**Thus ends the results of birth. Now begins the analysis of the First House (The Body).**

If the Lord of the Ascendant <note>term: Lagnesha - the planet ruling the rising sign</note> is in its sign of exaltation, a friendly division, or its own sub-division <note>term: navamsha - a 1/9th division of a sign used for fine-tuning strength</note>, and is joined with or aspected by beneficial planets, one should predict physical comfort and health. || 68 ||

When the Lord of the Ascendant is endowed with strength and placed in a cardinal or trine house <note>term: kendra-kona - the 1st, 4th, 7th, 10th or 5th, 9th houses, considered the strongest positions</note>, and is not aspected by malefic planets, the wise should predict physical well-being. || 69 ||

If the Sun is in the "Devaloka" division <note>A specific high-strength sub-division in the Shashtiamsha system</note>, the Lord of the Ascendant is strong, and the Lord of the Ninth House <note>term: Bhagyesha - the planet ruling the house of fortune</note> is in its sign of exaltation, the person will possess great fortune and fame. || 70 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant is extremely powerful, associated with beneficial divisions, and in its exaltation...

->**The Effects of the Ascendant Lord**<-

If the Lord of the Ascendant is joined by a friendly planet or is placed in its own <term>Navamsha</term><note>A one-ninth division of a zodiac sign, used to determine the hidden strength of a planet</note>, or if the Lord of a <term>Kendra</term><note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, considered the pillars of a horoscope</note> is joined with the Lord of the Ascendant, the person attains good fortune, fame, wealth, grain, and a long life. || 71 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant is joined with a <term>cruel planet</term><note>Malefics like Mars or Saturn</note>, they say the happiness of the body is destroyed. The same result occurs if the Lord is placed in a <term>house of destruction</term><note>The 6th, 8th, or 12th houses</note>; however, if it is aspected by a benefic planet, the result will be otherwise. || 72 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant is joined by the Lord of a <term>bad station</term><note>Dussthana: the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses</note> while in the Ascendant, the person will suffer from disease. But if the Lord of the Ascendant is weak yet placed in a <term>Kendra</term> or <term>Trikona</term><note>The 1st, 5th, or 9th houses</note>, they will not suffer from disease. || 73 ||

If the Lord of the sign occupied by the Lord of the Ascendant is placed in a bad station, the person will have a weak body. The destruction of the various houses (Lagna, etc.) is predicted when the Lords of the signs occupied by those house-lords are placed in bad stations. || 74 ||

When malefic planets are in the Ascendant, and <term>Gulika</term><note>A mathematical point or "shadow planet" considered highly malefic</note> is in a Trikona, or if the Lord of the Ascendant is joined with <term>Rahu</term><note>The North Node of the Moon, associated with obsession and deception</note> and Gulika, or if the Lord of the Ascendant is with a malefic and Rahu is in the Ascendant, there is a fear of deception and thieves. || 75 ||

Through the combination or aspect of <term>Saturn</term><note>Shani</note>, there is certain fear from deception, thieves, and kings. If Rahu is in the Ascendant along with <term>Mars</term><note>Kuja</note> and the son of the Sun (Saturn), the wise say there is a risk of <term>enlargement of the scrotum</term><note>Sanskrit: Brihad-beeja; often referring to hydrocele or hernia in ancient texts</note>. || 76 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 8th house (the house of death) with Rahu, or if <term>Mandi</term><note>Another malefic shadow planet similar to Gulika</note> is in the 8th house, the same should be said. If Rahu is in the Ascendant, Gulika is in a Trikona, and Mars is in the 8th house joined with Mandi, the same result follows. || 77 ||

If the Lord of the sign occupied by the Lord of the Ascendant is joined with Rahu, Mars, or Mandi, or if the Lord of the first <term>Amsha</term><note>A divisional portion of a sign</note> of the sign occupied by the Lord of the 8th house is joined with Rahu, there is a risk of scrotal enlargement. || 78 ||

If the "Son of the Earth" (Mars) is the Lord of the Ascendant and is placed in the Ascendant joined with or aspected by malefics, those who know the science say there will be a wound on the head caused by a stone or a sword. || 79 ||

If Saturn is so placed, there is a wound on the head caused by wind, fire, weapons, or a fall. When the Ascendant is within the first five <term>Ghatis</term><note>A unit of time; 5 Ghatis equals 2 hours</note>, this enlargement occurs, but not if it is in the half-Ascendant.

### Chapter 2

**80.** The ancient sages have said that if the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the time of birth</note> is a "shrunken" sign, the head of the native will be small or contracted; those who know the science of astrology affirm this.

**81.** When a "dry" planet <note>shushka-graha: planets associated with dryness, such as the Sun, Mars, or Saturn</note> occupies the Ascendant, or if the Ascendant itself is a dry sign, the sages declare that the body will be emaciated.

**82.** Likewise, if the Lord of the Ascendant is associated with a dry planet, or is situated in the house of dry planets, or if the Lord of the Ascendant has gone to the house of destruction <note>the 8th house</note> in a dry sign, the body suffers extreme and painful leanness.

**83.** If the lord of the sign occupied by the <term>Navamsha</term> <note>a one-ninth divisional chart used for fine-tuning predictions</note> lord of the Ascendant is placed with a dry planet, they say the body is thin. Furthermore, if the Ascendant is a dry sign and is joined by many malefic planets, the body is said to be frail.

**84.** If the Ascendant is a "watery" sign <note>Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces</note> and is joined by the best of the benefic planets, they cite this as an example of bodily stoutness (obesity). If the Lord of the Ascendant is a watery planet, possesses strength, and is joined by benefics, they say the body is well-nourished.

**85.** If the Lord of the Ascendant is situated in a watery sign, joined by benefics, and aspected by a watery planet; or if the Ascendant falls in a benefic sign, or if the lord of the Ascendant's Navamsha is in a watery sign—

**86.** —and if the Ascendant is free from the gaze of malefic planets and falls in a benefic sign; or if Jupiter is in the Ascendant or aspects it, and the Ascendant is a watery sign—

**87.** —and if it is joined by or aspected by the best of the benefic planets, they describe this as extreme obesity. If Saturn is in the Ascendant along with Rahu <note>the North Node of the Moon</note>, the wise say the person will suffer from <term>afflictions by spirits</term> <note>Pishacha-badha: historically interpreted as mental illness or external spiritual disturbances</note>.

**88.** If the Sun is in the Ascendant and is aspected by Mars, the native will suffer from respiratory issues, consumption (tuberculosis), abscesses, or abdominal tumors. If Mars is in the Ascendant and is aspected by Saturn and the Sun, the body may suffer injuries from swords or sharp weapons.

**89.** If Ketu <note>the South Node of the Moon</note> is in the Ascendant and is aspected by many malefic planets, there will certainly be fear from spirits and thieves. If the Ascendant is a "movable" sign <note>Chara-rashi: Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn</note>, or if its Lord is in a movable sign, the person born will be a wanderer.

The tendency to travel is predicted when the Ascendant or the Ascendant's Navamsha is in a movable sign. Fortune in foreign lands <note>Videsha-bhagya</note> occurs when the Ascendant is a movable sign and its Lord is also in a movable sign...

When the Sun <note>original: "Dineshe"</note> is in the Ascendant and is aspected by auspicious planets, and when the Lord of the Ascendant is delighted <note>in a favorable state</note> and in its sign of exaltation, those sages who are experts in this science say the person will possess excellent fame.
|| 1 || If the Lord of the Ascendant is associated with a malefic planet and Rahu <note>the North Node of the Moon</note>, and if a malefic planet is situated in the tenth house <note>the house of action/career</note>, or if a planet in its debilitation is in the Ascendant aspected by the Sun, then the person will be possessed of ill-repute.
|| 2 || When the Lord of the Ascendant is gaining strength in its upward movement <note>approaching exaltation</note> and the Lord of the ninth house <note>the house of fortune</note> possesses similar strength, the person born will be of celebrated fame, especially if associated with a benefic planet.
|| 3 || If the son of Bhrigu <note>Venus</note> is in the Ascendant, there is happiness in the first half of life; however, there is sorrow in the latter part if a malefic is in the fourth or fifth house.
|| 4 || If the Lord of the Ascendant is joined with a benefic, is in its exaltation, is placed in a quadrant or a trine <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, 10th or 5th, 9th houses</note>, and is aspected by a benefic—or if it is with the Lord of the tenth house in its own home—the person attains good fortune, fame, wealth, grain, and long life.
|| 5 || When the Lord of the Ascendant is exceedingly powerful, aspected by benefics, and situated in a quadrant while being observed by auspicious planets, it sweeps away death and bestows a very long life along with many virtues and great prosperity.
|| 6 || One who has no malefic planets in the quadrants, trines, or the eighth house, and whose Lord of the Ascendant and Jupiter <note>the Teacher of the Gods</note> are in quadrants, will enjoy various pleasures, perform virtuous deeds, and live for a hundred years free from disease.
|| 7 || If the Lord of the eighth house is more powerful than the Lord of the Ascendant, and malefic planets are in the quadrants or the sixth and eighth houses, the person's life is short; or if it is a medium lifespan, they reach the end of their life through great distress or crisis.
|| 8 || If Mercury, Venus, and Saturn are in the same division <note>Amsa</note> and are situated in the ninth house or the Ascendant, or if the Moon <note>the "cold-rayed one"</note> is in the sixth or eighth house...

When the Lord of the Family <note>original: "Kutumbesha"; the planet ruling the 2nd house of the zodiac</note> is joined by benefic planets, and is situated in the Paravata portion <note>term: Paravatamsha; a high-quality division in the Varga system indicating great strength</note>, and the Moon is in the house of wealth, the person is fortunate. || 21 ||

If the Lord of that house is in its sign of exaltation, a friend's sign, or its own home; or if the Lord of that house occupies a "Throne" division <note>term: Sinhasanamsha; a specific planetary strength</note> while in the Paravata portion and is aspected by Jupiter, the person born with such merit shall rule over three hundred people. || 22 ||

When the Lord of the Family is in its highest exaltation and is aspected by the teacher of the gods <note>Jupiter</note>, or if the house itself is so influenced, the person born becomes a protector of a thousand through their prowess. || 23 ||

If Jupiter <note>original: "Tridasheshapujya"</note> is in the "Throne" division, Venus is in the "Gopura" division <note>term: Gopuramsha; a specific strength grade</note>, and the Lord of Wealth is in the "Airavata" division <note>term: Airavatamsha; the highest strength grade, named after the celestial elephant</note> and is powerful, the person born will be a protector of countless people. || 24 ||

When the Lord of the Face <note>original: "Mukhesha"; the 2nd house also rules the face</note> is placed in a cardinal house <note>term: Kendra; the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note> and is aspected by benefic planets, or if a benefic planet is in the house of the face, that man will have a handsome countenance. || 25 ||

When the Lord of the Face is in a cardinal house, the person has a blooming face and is prosperous; this occurs when that Lord is in its exaltation, a friend's sign, or its own division, and occupies the "Gopura" portion. || 26 ||

If the house of the face is joined by malefic planets and its Lord is also joined by malefics, or if it goes to a sign of debilitation and is aspected by malefics, the person will have an ugly or distorted face. || 27 ||

That man will be prone to anger and sinful if the Lord of that house is joined by Gulika <note>note: a "shadow planet" usually considered inauspicious in Vedic astrology</note>. With many malefic combinations, he falls under the influence of low-born people or enemies. || 28 ||

When the Lord of the House of Speech <note>original: "Vaksthanapa"</note> is joined by a benefic and is in a trine or cardinal house, or is exalted, aspected by benefics, and joined with meritorious combinations, the person will be an eloquent speaker endowed with logic. || 29 ||

If the Lord of the House of Speech is joined by the Priest of the Gods <note>Jupiter</note> but is placed in the house of destruction <note>the 8th house</note>, the person is mute. This is the tradition regarding fathers and others as stated by the great sages, the knowers of many scriptures. || 30 ||

A person becomes very talkative when the Lord of that house is in a cardinal house, in the Paravata portion, and in its highest exaltation; or when Jupiter or Venus are in the "Throne" division, or Mercury <note>original: "Somasuta"; son of the Moon</note> is in the best division <note>term: Vargottama; occupying the same sign in both the main chart and the 9th divisional chart</note>. || 31 ||

If the Lord of the division occupied by the Lord of Speech is a benefic, is in its exaltation, and is joined by auspicious planets...

If the house of speech is joined with <term>Gulika</term><note>A mathematical point in the sky considered malefic, also called Mandi</note> and the Sun, and is aspected by malefic planets, the person born is dull-witted. || 34 ||

If Jupiter is in a <term>Kendra</term> or <term>Trikona</term><note>A 'trine' or auspicious house: 1st, 5th, or 9th</note> and Venus is in its sign of exaltation, or if Mercury is the Lord of the house of speech, the person becomes a mathematician. || 38 ||

If the Sun and Mars are in the house of speech and are aspected by Jupiter and Venus, and Mercury is in the <term>Paravatansha</term>, the person will be devoted to various forms of logic and reasoning. || 39 ||

If Jupiter is endowed with full strength and the Lord of that house is aspected by the Sun and Venus, this person will be a <term>Shabdika</term><note>A grammarian or linguist</note>. || 41 ||

If Mercury is the Lord of the house of speech and is in its exaltation, Saturn is in the <term>Gopuransha</term>, and Jupiter is in the <term>Simhasanansha</term><note>Literally 'throne-part', a high-status divisional strength</note>, the person will be a <term>Vedantajna</term><note>A knower of Vedanta philosophy</note>. || 42 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant <note>original: "Lagna-nātha"</note> is in the House of Gains <note>original: "Lābha-rāśi," the 11th house</note>, or if the Lord of Gains is situated in the Ascendant, the person will possess many treasures and great wealth. || 54 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant is the strongest of all planets, is placed in a quadrant <note>term: Kendra (the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, considered pillars of strength)</note>, and is joined by Jupiter <note>original: "Tridaśa-pūjita," literally 'the one worshipped by the thirty gods'</note>, and if the Lord of the House of Wealth is in a "Special Division" <note>term: Vaiśeṣikāṃśa (a high-quality planetary dignity achieved by being in favorable positions in multiple divisional charts)</note>, the ancient sages say the person earns wealth through their own courage and strength. || 55 ||

If the lord of the sign occupied by the ruler of the Navamsha <note>note: a 1/9th divisional chart used to assess hidden strength</note> associated with the Ascendant Lord is strong and is a friend to the Lord of Wealth, and is placed in a quadrant or a trine <note>term: Trikoṇa (the 1st, 5th, or 9th houses, considered auspicious)</note> or in its own sign, the person attains wealth through their own efforts in many ways. || 56 ||

If the Lord of Wealth is joined by the Lords of Gains and the Ascendant, and is placed in a trine or a quadrant, is aspected by benefics, and possesses temporal strength <note>original: "Kāla-bala"</note>, the person attains wealth through their own efforts during the middle part of life. || 57 ||

Wealth is attained in the latter part of life if the Lord of Wealth is in a sign joined by the Lord of the Ascendant and a benefic planet. The same is said if the Lord of that sign is in the Ascendant and the Lord of Gains is strong. || 58 ||

If the Lords of Wealth and the Ascendant are in the Third House, are endowed with strength, and are aspected by male planets, and are joined by the Lord of that house in a joyful state <note>note: "Prahrṛṣṭa," referring to a planet in a friendly or exalted sign</note> and in a "Special Division," the person attains wealth from a brother. || 59 ||

If the Lord of the Third House is in the House of Wealth, and the significator planet <note>term: Karaka (the planet representing a specific relative; for brothers, this is Mars)</note> is also there, and is aspected by or joined with the Lord of the Ascendant, the person attains wealth from a brother through special planetary divisions. || 60 ||

If the Lord of Wealth and the Lord of the Ascendant aspect each other, are in quadrants, and are in auspicious divisions, and are aspected by the Lords of the Ascendant and other benefics, the person attains wealth in many ways. || 61 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant aspects the Lord of Wealth, the person attains wealth through their own strength. If they are aspected by or joined with the Lord of the Third House and its significator, such wealth comes from that source. || 62 ||

If the strong Lord of Wealth is aspected by or joined with the Lord of Happiness <note>note: the ruler of the 4th house</note>, wealth comes from the mother. || 63 || When the Lord of Wealth <note>the ruler of the 2nd house</note> is situated in the House of Wealth, and is aspected by or conjoined with the Significator planet <note>Jupiter is the general significator for wealth</note>, and if these are aspected by or conjoined with the Lord of the Body <note>the Ascendant ruler</note> while in a Vaisheshika division, the person born shall obtain wealth from their brother. || 64 ||

When the Lord of the House of Sons <note>5th house ruler</note> and its Significator <note>Jupiter</note> are similarly placed, and the Lord of Wealth is strong, and if the Lord of the Ascendant is also strong and aspected or conjoined in a Vaisheshika division, wealth will come from one's children. || 65 ||

Wealth from the father is determined by the Significator <note>the Sun</note> and the House Lord <note>9th house ruler</note>; wealth from a Teacher <note>Guru</note> or through religious merit is also seen here. From the aspect or conjunction of the Lord of Action <note>10th house ruler</note> and its Significator, wealth comes through one's own giving and receiving, and through one's own fame. From the aspect or conjunction of the Lord of Gains <note>11th house ruler</note> and its Significator, the authorities say there is a great abundance of wealth. || 68 ||

If malefic planets are said to be in the House of Wealth and are strong, or if they are in debilitation, in an enemy's sign, or combust <note>too close to the sun</note>, and are aspected by or conjoined with other planets || 69 || then there will be a destruction of wealth through the significations of those respective House Lords. This sequence applies to brothers, relatives, children, enemies, and spouses. || 70 ||

When the Lord of the Ascendant is weak and joined with a malefic, and the Lord of Wealth is in the Twelfth House <note>the house of loss</note> joined with the Lord of the Day <note>the Sun</note>, or is in debilitation even if aspected by benefics, the King <note>the state or government</note> seizes the wealth of the person born. || 71 ||

If the Lord of Expenditure <note>12th house ruler</note> is in the House of Wealth, and the Lord of Gains is in the Twelfth House, and the Lord of Wealth is in a bad state or debilitated, there is a loss of wealth through Royal Punishment <term>Rāja-daṇḍa: legal fines or state seizure</term>. || 72 ||

If the Lord of Wealth is in the House of Destruction <note>8th house</note>, joined with a malefic and in a sign of debilitation, and is conjoined with the Significator of Royalty <note>the Sun</note>, there is a loss of wealth through Royal Punishment. || 73 ||

->**Combinations for Great Wealth and Debt**<-

...in a <term>Vaisheshika division</term><note>A specific strength-grading system in Vedic astrology where a planet gains power by being in its own or exalted sign in multiple divisional charts.</note>. If the Lord of the Ascendant is also joined in such a way, the person rises above his current status. || 98 || When Jupiter is joined with the Lord of the Ascendant, and the Lord of the 2nd House <note>The house of wealth</note> is in a <term>Vaisheshika division</term>, or placed in a <term>Kendra</term><note>Angular houses: 1, 4, 7, or 10</note> or <term>Trikona</term><note>Trinal houses: 1, 5, or 9</note>, the person attains wealth beyond expectations. || 99 ||

If the Lord of the 7th House is joined with the lord of the <term>Drekkana</term><note>A 10-degree subdivision of a sign</note> occupied by the Lord of the 10th House, and is placed in an <term>Airavata division</term><note>A very high strength grade where a planet is auspicious in nine divisional charts</note>, the person attains a hundred thousand pieces of wealth. || 100 ||

Two hundred thousand in wealth is attained when the four <term>Kendras</term> are occupied by benefic planets, and the Lord of the 2nd House is in a <term>Simhasana</term> or <term>Paravata division</term>. || 1 || One becomes the master of three hundred thousand if the Lords of the 11th <note>House of gains</note>, the Ascendant, and the 2nd House are in <term>Vaisheshika divisions</term> or joined with the <term>Mridu division</term><note>A "soft" or auspicious subdivision</note>. || 2 ||

Beyond that, one becomes a master of wealth when the Lords of the 2nd and 11th are in the houses of increase <note>Upachaya houses: 3, 6, 10, 11</note> or in <term>Kendras</term>, provided they and the Lord of the 9th <note>House of fortune</note> are strong. || 3 || If the Lord of the 9th is strong in a <term>Kendra</term> or <term>Trikona</term>, or joined with the Lord of the 11th, and placed in a <term>Vaisheshika division</term>, one attains a hundred thousand. || 4 ||

When the Lord of the Division <note>original: *Amshapati*; the planet ruling the specific zodiacal subdivision</note> is placed in its own sign or divisional strength, the person becomes skilled in war and an expert in conflict. || 33 ||

When the Lord of Valor <note>original: *Vikramadhipati*; the ruler of the 3rd house in a birth chart, which governs courage</note> is in its sign of exaltation, but placed in the house of destruction <note>the 8th house</note> and joined by malefic planets, and if it occupies a moveable sign or division, the person will be firm and resolute before the battle begins. || 34 ||

If the house of valor is owned by malefic planets and contains a malefic planet, and its Lord is similarly situated, the person will likewise be firm before the battle. || 35 ||

If the Lord of that house is in a "cruel" sixty-fold division <note>original: *Krura-shashtyamsa*; a specific technical subdivision of a sign considered harsh</note>, or is in its sign of debilitation, or is joined or aspected by malefic planets, the man becomes one who fights for the kingdom. || 36 ||

One is defeated in war if the Lord of Valor is in its exaltation but placed in the house of destruction, or if the significator <note>original: *Karaka*; the planet representing the specific matter</note> is weak or joined with a cruel sixty-fold division. || 37 ||

If the Lord of Valor is in the "Throne" division <note>original: *Simhasanamsa*</note>, or in the "Pigeon" or "Gate" divisions <note>original: *Paravata* and *Gopura*; these are technical measures of high planetary strength</note>, or in a "soft" division joined by the aspect of benefics, there will be a great celebration and the person will be an expert in war. || 38 ||

One desires war and is skilled in combat when the Lord of Strength <note>the 3rd Lord</note> is Mercury <note>original: *Somasuta*, literally "Son of the Moon"</note> in its exaltation, possessing full strength in the "Special" division <note>original: *Vaisheshikamsa*</note> or a soft division; otherwise, the opposite results occur. || 39 ||

If the Lord of Valor is joined with the Sun <note>original: *Bhanu*</note>, the person is brave; if with the Moon, they possess mental courage; <gloss>Alternative reading: joined with a benefic</gloss> if with Mars, they are dark-complexioned, dull-witted, and prone to anger; if with Mercury <note>original: *Saumya*</note>, they possess a virtuous and balanced intellect. || 40 ||

If joined with Jupiter <note>original: *Jiva*</note>, the person is endowed with courage and becomes an expert in the meaning of all treatises on wealth and politics <note>original: *Arthashastra*</note>. If joined with Venus <note>original: *Asphujit*</note>, the person is overcome by passion and becomes skilled in quarreling due to that anger. || 41 ||

If joined with Saturn <note>original: *Vasaranathaputra*, "Son of the Lord of the Day"</note> or with Rahu <note>original: *Phani*, "The Serpent"</note>, the person becomes dull; they appear firm on the outside but possess an internal dullness or misery. The same applies if joined with Ketu or Mandi <note>a mathematical point in the sky considered malefic</note>. || 42 ||

If Jupiter is in the Ascendant <note>the 1st house</note> joined with the Lord of Valor, the sages speak of a fear regarding four-legged animals <note>likely referring to cavalry or livestock in a military context</note>.

<note>1. There is a variant reading: "joined with a benefic."</note>

If a cruel planet <note>a malefic planet like Mars or Saturn</note> is situated in a sinful sign <note>a sign owned by a malefic</note>, they call it an axe to the ear <note>original: "tat-karṇa-kuṭhāram"; likely a metaphor for deafness or hearing afflictions</note>. || 53 || Thus ends the Third House.

### Now, the Fourth House

In the House of Kinship <note>the Fourth House, known as Bandhu-bhāva</note>, one should speak of relatives, home, mother, water, self-growth, and food. One also considers vehicles, the heart, shoulders, seats, beds, happiness, and deep waters. || 1 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant <term>Lagneśvara: the planet ruling the first house</term> is in the first house and the Lord of Happiness <term>Sukheśa: the ruler of the fourth house</term> is joined with the Lord of the Body <note>the Ascendant Lord</note>, the gain of a house is indicated. Through the aspect or conjunction of benefic planets, or if the planet is in its sign of exaltation, a friend's sign, or its own home and endowed with strength, this gain happens without effort. || 2 ||

When the Lord of the House is situated in a center <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</term>, is endowed with strength, and is aspected by a benefic, they say the gain of a residence is certain. If the Lord of the House is in a "Vaisheshika" division <note>a specific high-quality division in the ten-fold varga system</note> or in its highest exaltation, they say a residence will be gained. || 3 ||

Find the lord of the sign where the Lord of the Fourth House is placed in the divisional chart <note>Navamsha</note>; if that lord is in a center, one should predict the acquisition of a home. || 4 ||

If the Lord of Fortune <note>9th house ruler</note> is in a center and the Lord of the House is in its exaltation or a friendly sign, and if a planet in the Fourth House is also exalted, the home will be very multifaceted and grand. || 5 ||

If the third house is joined by a benefic and the Lord of the House is endowed with its own strength, and if that lord is fully powerful, the palace will be adorned with ramparts. || 6 ||

If the Lord of the House is in the "Simhasana" <note>Throne</note> or "Gopura" <note>Spire</note> divisions, or joined with the "Mridu" <note>Soft/Mild</note> division, that house will be adorned as a white mansion <note>original: "saudha-maṇḍitam"</note>. || 7 ||

If the Lord of the House is in the "Paravata" <note>Pigeon/Highest</note> division and is aspected by Jupiter and the Moon, or is in the "Gopura" division, one should predict a divine palace. || 8 ||

One should predict a house adorned with wonderful mansions and ramparts if the Lord of the House is joined with the Lord of Action <note>10th house ruler</note> in a center, or with the son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note>. || 9 ||

If the Lord of the House goes to the House of Destruction <note>the 8th or 12th house</note> and is aspected by a malefic, there will be the destruction of the home. If the lord of the divisional sign <note>Navamsha</note> occupied by the Lord of the House is also in a House of Destruction, the home will be lost. || 10 ||

If the Lord of the House of Kinship is a benefic and is aspected by benefic planets, or if the significator <term>Karaka: for the 4th house, usually the Moon or Mercury</term> is full of strength, the man will be honored by his relatives. || 11 ||

If Jupiter is in the House of Kinship and its lord is joined with a benefic...

If the fourth house is aspected <note>aspected: in astrology, when one planet "looks at" or influences another house or planet from a specific distance</note> by Jupiter, the person will have excellent relatives. || 12 || If the lord of the fourth house is placed in a <term>Kendra</term> <note>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, considered the "pillars" of a chart</note> or a <term>Trikona</term> <note>Trikona: the 1st, 5th, or 9th houses, considered auspicious "trines"</note>, is joined with the lord of that house, is in a <term>Vaisheshikansha</term> <note>Vaisheshikansha: a high-quality divisional strength where a planet gains many auspicious points</note>, and is free from the sight or company of "malefic" <note>malefic: planets like Mars or Saturn that traditionally cause challenges</note> planets, the person will be a benefactor to their relatives. || 13 ||

If Jupiter, Venus, or Mercury are in the fourth house, or if the fourth house is their own home, or if they aspect it, and if the house is in a "soft" <term>Shashtyansha</term> <note>Shashtyansha: a 1/60th division of a sign; "soft" or "mild" divisions indicate gentle results</note>, the person will be helpful to their kin. || 14 ||

A person is abandoned by their relatives if the lord of the fourth house is joined with malefic planets, or is in a cruel <term>Shashtyansha</term>, or is placed in a "debilitated" <note>debilitated: the sign where a planet is at its weakest</note> or enemy's sign. || 15 || If the fourth house, its lord, and its <term>Karaka</term> <note>Karaka: the "significator" or planet that naturally represents a topic; for the 4th house, this is usually the Moon or Mercury</note> are all joined with many malefic planets, one should say the person is despised by their relatives. || 16 ||

If the lord of the <term>Navamsha</term> <note>Navamsha: the 1/9th divisional chart, used to see the hidden strength of planets</note> occupied by the fourth lord is in a debilitated sign or is "combust" <note>combust: hidden by the sun's light, losing its power</note>, the person will perform acts that cause fear to their relatives. || 17 ||

One enjoys the company of relatives if the fourth lord is in a <term>Kendra</term> and is aspected by "benefic" <note>benefic: auspicious planets like Jupiter or Venus</note> planets, or is in a <term>Gopuramsha</term> <note>Gopuramsha: a specific high-strength position in the divisional charts</note> or a soft division. || 18 || If the fourth lord is in the 2nd, 11th, or a trine house, is aspected by benefics, or is in the division of a gentle planet, the person will be a benefactor to their kin. || 19 ||

One will always be at odds with relatives when the fourth house is occupied by malefic planets, or joined with debilitated or setting planets, and lacks the sight or company of benefics. || 20 || However, if any planet in the fourth house is in its "exaltation" <note>exaltation: the sign where a planet is at its maximum strength</note> or a friend's sign, and is aspected by Jupiter, the person will be honored by their relatives. || 21 ||

If the <term>Lagna</term> <note>Lagna: the Ascendant or rising sign</note> is a "movable" sign, and the fourth lord is also in a movable sign, and the significator is likewise placed, the person will own houses in many different places. || 22 || If these are in "fixed" signs, the house will be permanent. If the lord is in a benefic <term>Shashtyansha</term>, the person's residence will be stable. || 23 ||

As many malefic planets as are joined with the lords of the 2nd and 12th houses, that much destruction of the body and property may occur; however, if there is a benefic aspect, these faults are removed. || 24 || If the lords of the 2nd and 12th houses are in <term>Kendras</term> or <term>Trikonas</term>, then the entire house and temple <insert>property</insert> will be beautiful.

If the Lord of the Fourth House <note>original: "Sukhapa"</note> is well-placed and Jupiter <note>original: "Devapujita," literally 'worshiped by the gods'</note> is present, and if that planet is in a house of wealth or growth, the person will be happy. **47**
If the Fourth House is occupied by non-benefic planets, or if Jupiter is weak, or if the Lord of the Fourth is associated with malefic planets and lacks strength, the person will be miserable even if they possess wealth. **48**
Even if one has children, wealth, and kinsmen, they will be unhappy if a planet is in its "debilitation" <note>term: Neecha - the sign where a planet's influence is at its weakest</note>. If many malefic planets occupy the Fourth House, and its Lord is in an enemy sign or is "combust" <note>term: Mudha - a planet rendered invisible and weak by being too close to the Sun</note>, or is joined with Saturn <note>original: "Yamasunu," literally 'Son of Death'</note>, the person born will commit many sins. **53**

...the lord of the sign. || 57 || If the lord of the place of rivers <note>original: "sarit-sthana-adhipa"; likely referring to the lord of the 4th house or a watery sign</note> is joined with the Lord of the Ascendant <term>Lagnanatha: the planet ruling the first house of the self</term> in the fourth house, and is aspected by the Lord of the Tenth House, the person will fall into rivers, wells, or tanks. || 58 ||

The person will be struck by a stone if the Sun and Mars are in the fourth house, and it is aspected by or joined with the Lord of the Tenth or the lord of the place of rivers. || 60 ||

If the Lord of the Fourth House is joined with Rahu <note>the North Node of the Moon</note> and Saturn, and is aspected by Mars without any aspect from a benefic <term>benefic: a "good" planet like Jupiter or Venus</term>, the man will be afflicted by stones. || 61 ||

If the Moon or Venus is in a quadrant <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</term> joined with or aspected by a malefic, or is in a cruel division <note>original: "kruranshake"</note> or in a descending degree, this person commits incest with his mother. || 62 ||

If the Moon or the Sun is in a quadrant, aspected by or joined with a malefic, or if a malefic is in the fourth house under malefic aspect, the man born here will be a "mother-goer" <note>original: "matru-gami"; a term for incest</note>. || 63 ||

If the Lord of the Fourth House is aspected by or joined with a malefic and lacks the aspect of a benefic, and the Lord of the Ascendant is weaker than the Lord of the Seventh House, the man born will go to a woman who is like a mother to him. || 64 ||

Others say that union with a sister occurs when the Lord of the Seventh House is a malefic and situated in the fourth house, aspected by a malefic, or is in a cruel "sixtieth-division" <term>shashtyansha: a 1/60th division of a zodiac sign</term>. || 65 ||

If Saturn is in the fourth house, aspected by or joined with a malefic, or if the fourth house is a sign owned by a malefic planet and the planet there is in a cruel sixtieth-division, the same [sinful] results follow. || 66 ||

If the Moon is joined with the Lord of the Sixth House and Mars, situated in the fourth house and aspected by a malefic, or if the lord of the Navamsha <term>Navamsha: the 1/9th divisional chart</term> occupied by the Moon is similarly afflicted, they say there is a blemish upon the mother. || 67 ||

If the Lord of the Fourth House is joined with Rahu, a malefic, Saturn, and the Sun, the mother is attached to another man... <note>The text cuts off mid-sentence at the end of the page</note>

...and the same applies to the lord of the [relevant] house. || 68 ||

If the Lord of the Fourth House <note>The Fourth House (Sukha-bhava) represents the mother, home, and happiness</note> is situated in the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the rising sign at the moment of birth</term> with great strength, and is aspected by Jupiter, the Moon, Mercury, or Venus, and if it occupies a <term>Vaisheshika-amsha: a specific high-quality division of a sign</term> while being joined by or aspected by benefic planets, then the mother of the native will be a devoted and virtuous wife <note>original: "pativrata"</note>. || 69 ||

If the Moon is positioned in a similar manner but is joined by Rahu or Ketu <note>the North and South Lunar Nodes</note>, the mother may be inclined toward a man of lower status. If joined by Saturn, she may be inclined toward a laborer <note>original: "shudra-sakta"</note>; if joined by Mercury, toward a merchant <note>original: "vaishya-sakta"</note>. || 70 ||

If joined by the Sun, she is inclined toward the warrior class <note>original: "kshatriya-jati-sakta"</note>; if joined by Venus or Jupiter, toward the highest of the twice-born <note>original: "dvija-pungavaishcha," referring to the priestly or scholarly class</note>. If joined by Mars, the result should be declared in a similar manner according to the truth. || 71 ||

If the Lord of the Fourth House is joined by the Lord of the Sixth House <note>the house of enemies and obstacles</note> and is situated in the Ninth House <note>the house of fortune and the father</note>, it makes the father a paramour. Likewise, if the Lord of the Fourth is joined by the Lord of the Ninth and is situated in the Fourth House, it makes the father a paramour. || 72 ||

If the Lord of the Sixth House is joined with the Lords of the Ascendant, the Ninth, and the Fourth, the child is born of another <note>original: "parajata," meaning born of a father other than the mother's husband</note>. If the Lord of that house is joined with the Lord of its own division <note>amsha</note> and is aspected by malefic planets, the child is likewise born of another. || 73 ||

If the Fourth House is hemmed in by malefic planets, or its Lord or its <term>Karaka: the planetary significator (the Moon for the mother)</term> is aspected by benefics, yet the Lord of the Ascendant is weaker than the Lord of the benefic house, the one born at that time is born of another. || 74 ||

If the Ascendant is not aspected by Jupiter, or if the Moon is not aspected by Jupiter; or if the Moon is joined by the Sun, or the Moon is with a malefic and joined by the Sun... || 75 ||

If there are malefics and benefics in the Fourth House, and the Lord of the Ascendant is weak and joined by a malefic, and the Fourth House falls in a foreign division <note>paransha</note>, the person born then is born of another. || 76 ||

If the place of the mother <note>the Fourth House</note> is joined by benefics, and the significator <note>the Moon</note> is joined by benefics, or if the Lord of the Fourth is very strong, one should predict a long life for the mother. || 77 ||

If the Moon or Venus is very strong and aspected by Mercury, and joined with good fortune, and if the <term>Kendras: the four angular houses (1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th)</term> from the Fourth House are filled with benefics, they declare a long life <note>original: "dirghayu"</note> for the mother.

## Now, the House of Children

From the house of children <note>the Fifth House</note>, the wise man should indicate children, intelligence, and ministers; likewise, counsel, food, and the state of the father. He should also determine the entry into the heart and stomach, and the power of discernment. || 1 ||

One should speak of the concerns regarding children and others through the lords of the houses of spouse <note>7th</note>, children <note>5th</note>, and fortune <note>9th</note>, along with Jupiter <note>the significator of children</note>. Likewise, intelligence is known through Mercury <note>original: Somasuta, "son of the Moon"</note> and the Fifth House; and the father is known through the Fifth House, the Ninth House, and the Sun. || 2 ||

If the Sun is in the Fourth House <note>the house of happiness</note>, the father's wealth passes away. If the Moon is in the Fifth House, it indicates the death of the mother. If the Fifth House is occupied by a benefic planet or has a favorable aspect and conjunction, and its lord is similarly placed, it certainly grants a son. || 3 ||

When the house of children, or its lord, or Jupiter is aspected by a benefic, or is in conjunction with a benefic, the attainment of a son is without doubt. || 4 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant <term>Lagnesha: the planet ruling the rising sign</term> is placed in the house of children, and the Lord of the Fifth House is endowed with strength, and Jupiter is at full strength, the attainment of a son is without doubt. || 5 ||

If Jupiter is the lord of the house of children and is endowed with full strength, or is aspected by the Lord of the Ascendant, the attainment of a son is without doubt. || 6 ||

If Jupiter is in a <term>Vaisheshikansha: a specific high-quality division in the ten-fold or sixteen-fold varga system</term>, and the Lord of the Fifth House is similarly situated, or aspected by a benefic planet, one should predict the attainment of a son. || 7 ||

If the Lord of Wealth <note>the 2nd House lord</note> is in the house of children endowed with full strength and is aspected by Jupiter <note>original: Devadruguru, "the teacher of the gods"</term>, the attainment of a son is without doubt. || 8 ||

If the lords of the Ascendant and the Fifth House are in conjunction, or aspect each other, or are placed in each other's signs, the attainment of a son is without doubt. || 9 ||

If the lords of the Ascendant and the Fifth House are in a quadrant <note>houses 1, 4, 7, or 10</note> and joined with benefic planets, and the Lord of the Family <term>Kutumbesha: the ruler of the 2nd house</term> is powerful, the attainment of a son is without doubt. || 10 ||

If the lord of the sign occupied by the Lord of the Fifth House is joined with a benefic, or aspected by a benefic, the attainment of a son is without doubt. || 11 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the house of the spouse <note>7th</note>, and the Lord of Fortune <note>9th</note> is with the spouse, and the Lord of the Second House is in the Ascendant, the attainment of a son is without doubt. || 12 ||
