### The Results of Planetary Periods

During the ripening of a **"Blazing"** <term>Pradipta: a planet in its sign of exaltation</term> planet's period, one attains sovereignty over the earth, energy, heroism, wealth, and vehicles. One gains a wife, children, happiness, and the respect of kinsmen; one receives honors from kings and acquires sacred knowledge. || 6 ||

In the ripening of the period of a **"Healthy"** <term>Svastha: a planet in its own sign</term> planet, one remains healthy and gains happiness through wealth received from the king. One attains knowledge, fame, affection, greatness, a spouse, wealth, land, children, and the path of righteousness. || 7 ||

In the ripening of the period of a planet endowed with **"Joy"** <term>Mudita</term>, one gains clothing, land, perfumes, children, wealth, and courage. One finds interest in listening to the ancient histories <note>original: "Purana"</note> and religious duties, and acquires music, charity, vehicles, and excellent ornaments. || 8 ||

During the ripening of the period of a **"Peaceful"** <term>Shanta</term> planet, one attains happiness and courage, as well as sons, a wife, and vehicles. One engages in the humor of learning and the study of the scriptures of righteousness, gaining great wealth and the respect of the lords of the land. || 9 ||

Fall from one's position and opposition from kinsmen occur in the ripening of the period of a **"Deficient"** <term>Hina</term> planet. Such a person lives a life of contemptible and low conduct, abandoned by people and afflicted by passions or diseases. || 10 ||

In the ripening of the period of a planet endowed with **"Sorrow"** <term>Duhkhita/Kshubha</term>, one constantly encounters various kinds of misery. One goes to foreign lands, is separated from kinsmen, and suffers fear from thieves and kings while being falsely accused. || 11 ||

In the ripening of the period of an **"Impaired"** <term>Vikala</term> planet, one suffers impairment and mental affliction. Specifically, there is the death of the father and others, and distress regarding one's wife, children, vehicles, clothing, or loss to thieves. || 12 ||

In the ripening of the period of a **"Wicked"** <term>Khala</term> planet, one encounters quarrels, separation, and the loss of one's father. One faces the enmity of the people and the constant loss of wealth and land at the hands of one's own kinsmen...

During the ripening of the period <term>Dasha-vipaka; the time when a planet's influence bears fruit</term> of the Thousand-Rayed One <note>original: "Sahasrabhanu," an epithet for the Sun</note>, there is great suffering. It causes the loss of parents, distress to wife and children, and emaciation caused by thieves, fire, or the king. || 19 || If the Sun is aspected by a benefic planet, he brings about the splendor of knowledge, sacrifices, wife, children, and eloquent speech. He bestows radiance, majesty, the pleasure of amorous play, the happiness of parents, and honor from the king. || 20 || Even if the Sun is placed in a center <term>Kendra; the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a birth chart</term>, during the ripening of his period, one suffers punishment from the king. One faces displacement from one's position, separation from kinsmen, the failure of agriculture, and the exhaustion of wealth. || 21 || During the ripening of the Sun when placed in a trine <term>Trikona; the 1st, 5th, or 9th houses</term>, there is confusion of the mind and dishonor from the king. At that time, one suffers the loss of happiness, the death of the father, and failure in one's duties and actions. || 22 || The period of the Sun in its sign of exaltation <term>Uchcha-amshaka; the highest point of planetary strength</term> provides a livelihood, great wealth born of constant majesty, various refined amusements, the pleasure of amorous play, and the constant gain of women and garments—yet also the destruction of the paternal clan. || 23 || In the period of the Sun joined with its sign of debilitation <term>Nicha-amshaka; the weakest point of planetary strength</term>, there is travel to foreign lands for the sake of wife, wealth, or land. Abandoned by people and despised by kinsmen, one suffers from mental disorders, fever, and urinary diseases. || 24 || At the beginning of the Sun's period, there is sorrow and decline caused by the father's illness and mental anxiety. In the middle, there is loss of cattle and wealth, and at the end, greatness in knowledge. || 25 || One suffers loss of wealth during the ripening of the period of the Sun in the sixth house, along with a web of extreme sorrows. One may suffer from chronic diseases arising from the spleen or consumption, or perhaps difficulty in urination or diabetes. || 26 || In the period of the Sun in the eighth house, there is physical distress or danger from fire. One suffers from quartan ague <note>a fever that recurs every four days</note>, eye disorders, cough, fever with diarrhea, and loss of one's position. || 27 || If the period of the Sun in the twelfth house occurs, there is loss of treasury and wealth, emaciation, and the loss of wife, kinsmen, children, and land, or the death of parents.

->**The Results of the Sun's Period**<-

The results <note>Sanskrit: *phalam*; the karmic fruits or outcomes</note> are as follows: Wandering from place to place, danger from poison, fear of the king <note>In a modern context, this refers to legal troubles or government authorities</note>, and ailments of the feet. There will be disputes in assemblies regarding learning and debates, and suffering for cattle and horses. || 28 ||

If the Sun is situated in the second house <note>Sanskrit: *dhanastha*; the house of wealth and speech</note>, it brings about the birth of a son but also calamities. It causes distress, the sorrow of separation from kinsmen, quarrels, harshness of speech, and anger. || 29 ||

There will be the loss of a wife, loss of wealth, and fear of the king. One's land, sons, vehicles, and clothing—all these may face destruction. However, if the Sun is joined by a benefic planet <note>A "benefic" is a naturally auspicious planet like Jupiter or Venus</note>, these negative results should not be predicted. || 30 ||

During the period of the Sun when it is endowed with valor <note>Sanskrit: *vikrama*; likely referring to the third house</note>, one experiences great courage and happiness. There is honor from the king and the acquisition of wealth, yet also enmity with brothers and misfortunes. || 31 ||

During the period of the Sun situated in the house of happiness <note>The fourth house, governing home and comforts</note>, there is a loss of enjoyments, wealth, servants, and spouse. There is the destruction of fields and lands, fall from one's position, or loss of vehicles, as well as danger from thieves, poison, fire, and weapons. || 32 ||

During the period of the Sun even when associated with a spouse <note>Likely referring to the seventh house</note>, there is illness for the wife or even death. One receives poor food—meals that are badly cooked and lacking in milk, curds, and ghee <note>clarified butter, a staple of a high-quality diet</note>. || 33 ||

During the period of the Sun situated in the house of action <note>Sanskrit: *karmasthasya*; the tenth house of career and public life</note>, one attains a kingdom and wealth, and possesses courage. There is success in industry, accompanied by fame, victory in disputes, and honor from the king. || 34 ||

In the ripening of the period of the Sun situated in the house of gains <note>The eleventh house</note>, there is the acquisition of wealth and the gain of auspicious deeds. There is success in industry, happiness from sons and wife, and physical comfort through vehicles, ornaments, and clothing. || 35 ||

Whatever substances were mentioned for a planet in the "Chapter on Terminology" <note>Sanskrit: *Samjna-adhyaya*</note>, and whatever was taught regarding its "Livelihood" <note>Sanskrit: *Karma-jiva*; the profession indicated by the planet</note>, and whatever arises from its house position, aspects, and conjunctions—all of those things should be applied to that planet's period. || 36 ||

When the Sun is superior in positional strength <note>Sanskrit: *sthana-bala*</note>, one gains wealth from agriculture, cattle, land, vehicles, and clothing. One becomes radiant, receives great honor from the king, and is joined with the wealth of others. In its ripening <note>the fulfillment of the period</note>, one obtains bedding, clothing, and the like, an improvement in physical appearance, and great fame.

# Chapter 13: The Effects of the Sun's Period

<margin>V. Vi. A. 13</margin>
<margin>Page 56</margin>

...ornaments, the company of beloved kinsmen, and the great merit of bathing in holy waters. **(36)** When the Sun is devoid of **Positional Strength** <note>Sthana-bala: strength derived from the planet's zodiacal placement</note>, during its maturity <note>the period when the planet's influence is active</note>, there is a loss of wealth. One suffers from displacement from one's position, opposition from relatives, and the sorrow of wandering from one's own country to foreign lands. **(37)**

When the Lord of the Day <note>The Sun</note> is endowed with **Directional Strength** <note>Dig-bala: the Sun is strongest in the 10th house/South</note>, one gains wealth and happiness from distant directions. One attains fame, money, and land from those specific directions; otherwise, such results are not found here. **(38)**

When the Sun is strongest in **Temporal Strength** <note>Kala-bala: strength derived from the time of birth, such as day or night</note>, its maturity brings success in agriculture, land, and wealth, as well as professional success and honors from the king. If the Sun is weak in temporal strength, there is destruction. **(39)**

When the Sun possesses **Natural Strength** <note>Naisargika-bala: the inherent brightness of the planet; the Sun is naturally the strongest</note>, everything comes naturally: vehicles, wealth, ornaments, fine clothes, and physical well-being. If the Sun is weak <note>original: "hine ravau"</note>, there is fear of thieves, kings, and fire. **(40)**

When the Sun is endowed with **Motional Strength** <note>Cheshta-bala: strength derived from the planet's movement/speed</note>, one attains happiness and wealth through one's own efforts. One receives honor from the king, happiness from children and spouse, and gains through agriculture, vehicles, and clothing. If weak, these are lacking. **(41)**

When the Sun is joined with the strength and aspect of other planets, all happiness comes unexpectedly during its maturity. If it is devoid of this, everything is destroyed. **(42)**

During the period of a Sun placed in a **Cruel Sixty-fold Division** <note>Krura-shashtyansha: a specific 1/60th division of a sign ruled by a malefic influence</note>, there is displacement, or fear of kings and thieves. There is excessive anger, headaches, and the loss of the father or paternal relatives. **(43)**

During the period of a Sun placed in a **Mild Sixty-fold Division** <note>Mridu-shashtyansha: a 1/60th division ruled by a benefic influence</note>, one acquires soft clothes and ornaments. One attains two names <note>perhaps a title or alias</note>, is well-honored by kings, and gains knowledge of **Vedanta** <note>philosophical systems</note>, **Agamas** <note>scriptures</note>, and **Dharmashastra** <note>treatises on law and ethics</note>. **(44)**

During the maturity of the Sun placed in the **Paravata Division** <note>Paravatansha: a high-quality divisional strength where a planet occupies its own or exalted sign in six different vargas</note>, one attains great fame. There is honor from kinsmen and the ruler of the land, and the gain of children, good friends, and a spouse. **(45)**

The results arising from the Sun being in its sign of exaltation are said to manifest first, while other results follow...

The results arising from the aspects of the planets <note>original: "khecharadrishti"; the influence one planet exerts over another by "looking" at it from a specific distance</note> should be placed in the middle of the house of results; the same should be applied here for the malefic planets. || 46 ||

During the maturation of the period of the Sun <note>original: "Bhanu"</note>, if it is joined with the third of a sign <note>term: Drekkana (a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign)</note> associated with the Serpent <note>original: "Bhujangam-tryamsha"; the 2nd or 3rd decan of certain signs associated with snakes</note>, there is fear of poison. Likewise, if joined with the third of a sign associated with the Noose <note>original: "Pasha-tryamsha"</note>, one suffers from the wrath of kings, fire, loss of social standing, and manifold miseries. || 47 ||

Even if the Lord of Day <note>The Sun</note> is in its highest exaltation, if it resides in a debilitated division <note>term: Navamsha; a 1/9th sub-division where a planet's strength is further refined</note>, there will be loss of wife and wealth. According to the words of the Sages, there will be opposition from one's own family and kinsmen, as well as from the father and others. || 48 ||

The Sun, even if situated in its sign of debilitation, produces great happiness if it is joined with an exalted division. It bestows the burden of ruling a kingdom, though it may cause slight distress at the very end of the period. || 49 ||

**Thus end the results of the Sun's period. Now begin the results of the Moon's period.**

During the maturation of the period of the Moon <note>original: "Nishakara," literally 'the night-maker'</note>, even if it is in its highest exaltation, one attains flowers and fine garments. One reaches greatness, gains a spouse, increases wealth, and enjoys the pleasures of the mind and children. || 1 ||

Upon the arrival of the period of the Moon, even when exalted, one gains children, a wife, and wealth; yet there is also distress regarding sweet foods, drinks, clothes, and ornaments, as well as travel to foreign lands and opposition from one's own people. || 2 ||

The "ascending" period of the Moon <note>original: "Arohini"; referring to the Moon increasing in strength or moving toward its exaltation point</note> brings happiness and fame through women, children, wealth, and clothing. It bestows sovereignty, pleasant meals, the worship of gods, and the satisfaction of priests <note>original: "Bhusura," literally 'gods of the earth'</note>. || 3 ||

During the "descending" time of the Moon <note>original: "Avarohaka"; the Moon decreasing in strength</note>, there is a loss of happiness regarding women, children, friends, and clothing. One suffers from mental afflictions, opposition from kinsmen, and falls into a lake or pit due to thieves, fire, or kings. || 4 ||

Upon the arrival of the period of the Moon, if it is in a debilitated division, there is loss of various types of wealth. One encounters poor food, service to a wicked king, mental distress, and reproach. || 5 ||

In the period of a Moon situated in its "Root Trine" <note>term: Mula-trikona; a specific favorable position in a sign, second only to exaltation</note>, one obtains wealth from the king, land, sons, and a wife. One gains honors and garments from the sovereign, happiness from the mother, and is intent on the play of amorous delights. || 6 ||

Without much effort, one gains vehicles and territory, receives honors from kings, and possesses many means of transport.

|| 40 || When the Moon is endowed with the strength of aspects <term>Drik-bala: strength gained when a planet is viewed by beneficial planets</term>, through the compassionate glance of a king, one attains all manner of fortune, happiness, the desire to help others, and the fulfillment of one's heart's longings.

One faces the loss of wife and sons, the wrath of the protector of the earth <note>the government or king</note>, disputes over knowledge, and quarrels with the public.

|| 42 || During the period of the Moon placed in a "soft" or auspicious sixtieth division, one gains many sons. There is the acquisition of servants and wealth, victory, happiness, fame, and especially the attainment of deep learning.

One enjoys the pleasures of learning, happiness, the worship of the gods, and the merit of bathing in holy waters.

|| 44 || A Moon joined with a cruel decanate <term>Drekkana: a 1/3rd division of a sign</term> indicates illness. One's actions become joined with sin, and there is the harassment of cows and priests <note>original: "Go-Brahmana," traditionally representing the sacred and intellectual pillars of society</note>.

|| 45 || First, the results of the house position were told, then the results arising from planetary strength. After that, the results arising from the divisional placements and the inherent nature of the planet were given.

## Now, the Period of Mars <note>Sanskrit: Bhauma-dasha; Mars is associated with energy, fire, and warfare.</note> ##

During the period of the Son of Earth <note>original: "Bhunandana," a name for Mars</note> when he is at his highest exaltation, a person gains land and wealth, and achieves victory in battle. He receives great honors from kings and enjoys the pleasures of siblings, wife, children, and eloquent speech. || 1 || Indeed, during the period of the Son of Earth <note>original: "Dharanisuta," another name for Mars</note> when he has reached his highest point, one attains a kingdom or wealth from a sovereign. He experiences the gathering of land, wealth, wife, children, and kinsmen, and enjoys riding vehicles and traveling to special foreign lands. || 2 ||

The ascending period of the Son of Earth brings happiness and makes one worthy of worship by the ruler of men. It brings leadership, courage, the fulfillment of heart's desires, increasing good fortune, and a multitude of cows, elephants, and horses. || 3 || However, during the descending period of the Son of Earth, there is the loss of position and wealth, and suffering from strife and anger. One suffers the hardship of living in foreign lands, opposition from one's own kin, and fear from thieves, fire, and kings. || 4 ||

Even when the Son of Earth is in his sign of debilitation <note>the weakest zodiacal position</note>, during his period, one protects their kin through base occupations. There is poor food, the loss of cows, elephants, and horses, the loss of one's own relatives, and trouble from kings, fire, and thieves. || 5 || During the period of Mars situated in his Root-Trine <note>term: Mula-trikona; a specific favorable position in a zodiac sign that is stronger than a regular sign but less than exaltation</note>, one obtains sweet food, drinks, garments, and ornaments. One enjoys listening to the ancient scriptures <note>Puranas</note> and religious duties, happiness from brothers and others, and gains from agriculture. || 6 ||

In the ripening of the period of the Son of Earth when he is in his own sign, one gains wealth and land. He attains lordship over a place, comfortable vehicles, two names <note>likely a title or an alias of honor</note>, happiness from brothers, and the attainment of pleasure. || 7 || During the period of the Son of Earth when he has gone to the sign of a great enemy, there is suffering from quarrels and the like. During the period of Mars when it is joined with its highest point of exaltation <note>original: "ucchāṃśa"; the point where a planet is strongest</note>, the individual attains their heart's desires, victory, and happiness. The king gains a powerful female servant <note>likely referring to an influential attendant or concubine</note> and achieves prominence, like a fragrant lotus. [31]

In the period of Mars when it is in its lowest point <note>original: "nīcāṃśa"; debilitation</note> or joined with low influences, there is an extreme failure of duties and actions. There is loss of wealth, punishment from the ruler, and the person becomes solely devoted to the pleasures of the stomach and genitals. [32]

In the <term>period of Mars</term> <note>original: "Bhauma-dasha"</note>, at the beginning, one experiences various losses of wealth and honor. In the middle, the wise should predict fear from fire, rulers, and thieves. [33] At the end, there is separation from brothers, and issues regarding children, wealth, or wife, as well as chronic internal diseases <note>original: "gulma"; often referring to abdominal tumors or severe bloating</note> and the like. Even if these do not occur in the <term>Mars period</term>, one should specifically describe them when they align with the planet's current transit. [34]

During the ripening of the period of <term>Mars</term> when it is endowed with positional strength, there is happiness regarding wealth and one's spouse. One attains gains of position, happiness, fame, and valor, and achieves success in their endeavors through this period. [35]

However, <term>Mars</term> <note>original: "Kuja"</note> devoid of positional strength causes a fall from one's own rank. Life is sustained certainly through the practice of usury <note>original: "kusīda-vṛttyā"; lending money at interest</note>. [36]

In the period of <term>Mars</term> endowed with directional strength <note>original: "dig-vīrya"; strength gained by being in the South</note>, one gains wealth from the king and shows prowess in battle. There are gains of cattle, land, agriculture, clothing, and vehicles, and one's fame and power spread to the ends of the earth. [37]

In the <term>period of Mars</term> endowed with temporal strength <note>original: "kāla-vīrya"; strength gained by the time of day or night</note>, one attains desired objects and reaches happiness. There are gains of silk garments, gems, and pearls, as well as colorful clothes, agriculture, cattle, and elephants. [38]

In the period of <term>Mars</term> endowed with natural strength <note>original: "nisarga-vīrya"</note>, by the compassionate glance of kings, one receives all fortunes, children, friends, and relatives, as well as cattle, land, ornaments, clothing, and physical well-being. [39]

Naturally, there may be loss of position, wealth, and eyesight, an excess of bile <note>original: "pitta"; one of the three humors in Ayurvedic medicine</note>, and the eating of contemptible food. In the period of <term>Mars</term>, one may have deformed nails, be harmful to the father, and there is physical suffering for one's siblings. [40]

# Chapter 14 of the Sarvartha Chintamani
<page-num>71</page-num>
-> Section on the Period of Mars <-

...at that time, there is great fear. One suffers from thieves, fire, and serpents, as well as exile in the forest and <term>loss of position</term><note>Original: padachyutim; refers to being demoted or losing one's professional standing</note>. || 41 || During the period of Mars, if he is endowed with strength of vision, one receives the compassionate side-glance of kings. There is the acquisition of all types of fortune, children, friends, and kinsmen, as well as land, cattle, ornaments, apparel, and physical comfort. || 42 || 

During the period of Mars when he is associated with a <term>cruel sixtieth-division</term><note>Original: krura-shashtyansha; a specific technical calculation in Vedic astrology where a sign is divided into 60 parts, some of which are considered 'malefic' or cruel</note>, there is extreme suffering, imprisonment, and the destruction of all wealth. || 43 || 

During the period of Mars associated with a <term>gentle sixtieth-division</term><note>Original: saumya-shashtyansha; the auspicious divisions of the 60-fold chart</note>, auspiciousness occurs: marriage ceremonies, initiations, sacrifices, and being a benefactor to all. || 44 || 

During the period of Mars associated with <term>Paravata and other vargas</term><note>Original: paravatadi; refers to high-quality planetary dignities where a planet occupies many auspicious divisional charts</note>, there is great happiness, acquisition of land, wealth, a spouse, prosperity, vehicles, and fine food. || 45 || 

During the period of Mars associated with a <term>cruel decanate</term><note>Original: krura-dreshkana; a 10-degree division of a sign</note>, there is mental agony, fetters, fear of poison, and even being bound by ropes. || 46 || 

Even if the <term>Son of the Earth</term><note>Original: dharasunu; a common epithet for the planet Mars</note> is in his sign of exaltation, if he is in a debilitated subdivision, his ripening period brings the death of a brother and fear from kings, fire, and poison. || 47 || 

Conversely, even if the Son of the Earth is in his sign of debilitation, if he is in an exalted subdivision, his ripening period brings the increase of land, spouse, wealth, children, and friends. || 48 || 

**Thus ends the Period of Mars.**

-> Now begins the Period of Mercury <-

During the period of the <term>Son of the Moon</term><note>Original: somatmanaja or shashankasunu; epithets for the planet Mercury</note> when he is at his highest exaltation, the person becomes endowed with wealth, attains fame, and finds happiness. They gain wisdom, renown, leadership over people, and celebrate great festivals involving women, children, land, and wealth. || 1 || 

The period of the Son of the Moon, when placed in his exaltation sign, brings greatness, wealth, and comfort. It provides nourishment to the body, abundance of grain, children, cattle, horses, and intoxicated elephants, accompanied by the sound of the <term>mridanga drum</term><note>A traditional barrel-shaped double-headed drum</note>. || 2 || 

The <term>ascending period</term><note>Original: arohini; refers to a period where the planet's strength is increasing</note> of Mercury, when attained, brings sacrificial festivals and herds of cows, bulls, and horses. One gains sweet food, ornaments, apparel, and vehicles, and finds success in commerce, land dealings, and acts of charity. || 3 || 

However, the <term>descending period</term><note>Original: avarohini; refers to a period where the planet's strength is waning</note> of the Son of the Moon brings great hardship and sorrow...

...not lacking in association with the wives of others; there is great suffering here from fear of kings, fire, and thieves. || 4 || <note>original: "nṛpāgnicorairbhayam" - a common Vedic astrological formula for external threats during difficult periods.</note> During the period of the Son of the Moon <note>original: "Candrātmaja," a name for Mercury</note> situated in its sign of debilitation <term>Debilitation: the zodiacal sign where a planet is at its weakest influence</term>, one is bereft of knowledge and abandoned by one's own people. In the period of the Benevolent One <note>original: "Saumya," another name for Mercury</note> when placed in its Root Trine <term>Moolatrikona: a specific favorable placement in a sign, stronger than an ordinary friendly sign but less than exaltation</term>, there is a great kingdom, the bringing of happiness, and fame. Upon attaining the period of the Son of the Moon <note>original: "Shashankasunu," Mercury</note> while in its own sign, there is wealth, grain, and prosperity. One acquires success in commerce, cattle, land, sons, and wealth, as well as wives, soft food, drink, garments, and ornaments. || 7 ||

When the Son of the Moon is in an enemy's sign, there is fear of enemies and fear arising from the anger of the king. One is bereft of learning, serves those of low lineage, eats poor food, and suffers the loss of wife, sons, and wealth. || 8 ||

In the ripening <note>original: "pāke," referring to the fruition of the dasha period</note> of the Son of the Moon when it has gone to the sign of a great enemy, there is dispute and sorrow. There is the ruin of one's industry, opposition from one's own people, obstacles to sacrifices, and the destruction of auspicious works. || 9 ||

In the period of the Son of the Moon in a friend's sign, there is the coming of wealth and happiness. One attains two names <note>original: "nāmadvaya," possibly referring to a title or honorific</note> and composes prose and verse marked with one's own name. || 10 ||

The period of the one who has gone to the sign of a great friend brings greatness. There is happiness from the friendship of the king, wealth, sons, wives, and honor from kinsmen. || 11 ||

The period of the Son of the Moon even when in a neutral sign <note>original: "samakṣagasya"</note> brings happiness, grain, sons, and garments. However, it also causes a fall from one's kingdom, obstacles, lack of specialized knowledge, and diseases such as boils or pustules. || 12 || <note>original: "piṭikādirogam" - skin eruptions or inflammatory ailments.</note>

In the period of the Benevolent One <insert>Mercury</insert> conjoined with a debilitated planet, there is extreme difficulty. There is wandering from one's position, destruction of kinsmen, ruin of one's work, and mental affliction. || 13 ||

In the period of the Benevolent One conjoined with an exalted planet <term>Exaltation: the zodiacal sign where a planet's influence is at its highest potential</term>, there is great happiness. There is an increase in fortune, good learning, commerce, and the activities of cattle-rearing and agriculture. || 14 || The wise... conjoined with a malefic...

# Sanketa Chintamani, Chapter 14
<page-num>72, 14</page-num>

->**The Effects of Mercury's Period**<-

...even in its division, one encounters sin. There is the destruction of fields, wealth, wife, children, agriculture, cattle, and land. || 15 || During the ripening <note>original: "paripāke"; refers to the fruition of a planetary period</note> of Mercury <note>original: "vidaḥ"; a name for Mercury meaning 'the learned one'</note>, if it is joined with a benefic planet, there is great happiness. One attains royal success <term>Rajayoga: a combination of planets indicating power or high status</term>, comfort, fame, and joy from wife, children, and the king. || 16 ||

During the period-ripening of the Son of the Moon <note>original: "shashankasuno"; Mercury</note>, if aspected by a benefic planet, one gains great fame. There is the emergence of playfulness in learning, honor from the king, and a splendorous majesty accompanied by renown. || 17 || If the Son of the Moon is aspected by a malefic planet, there is a loss of grain and separation from kinsmen. One travels to foreign lands, falls from one's position, and suffers through the service of others, quarrels, and hardships. || 18 ||

The period of the Son of the Moon, when placed in a center <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a horoscope, considered pillars of strength</term>, brings friendship with kings, wealth, grain, a wife, and sons. One attains the performance of sacrifices and similar rituals, honor from the king, fame, and the acquisition of fine food, drinks, beds, clothes, and ornaments. || 19 ||

When the Son of the Moon is in the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term>, his period brings honor from the king and fortune gained through agriculture. One travels on roads announced by the sound of kettledrums and similar instruments, or performs ablutions at holy pilgrimage sites, becoming famous in the world. || 20 ||

In the period of Mercury situated in the second house <note>original: "vittaga"; the house of wealth and speech</note>, one attains knowledge and great renown. Equal to the fortune of a king, one attains a position of leadership in the royal palace. || 21 ||

During the ripening of the period of the Son of the Moon situated in the third sign <note>the third house</note>, one encounters dullness of intellect. There is anxiety, chronic abdominal disease <note>original: "gulmaroga"; often interpreted as enlargement of the spleen or various internal growths</note>, distress regarding food, yet also honor from the king. || 22 ||

When the Son of the Moon is situated in the fourth house <note>original: "hibuka"; a term derived from the Greek 'hypogeion'</note>, the arriving period brings the destruction of house and grain. One is deprived of happiness and the like; it may bring the death of the lord of the fourth house, the failure of industry, or a fall from one's position. || 23 ||

If the Son of the Moon is in the fifth house, one may possess a cruel intellect and face extreme difficulties. Even with a lowly occupation, through the service of the king, one attains wealth and prosperity through great effort. || 24 ||

During the period of Mercury <note>original: "Saumya-daye"; Mercury is called 'Saumya' or 'the Gentle One' in Sanskrit</note> when it is placed in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth houses, a person suffers from many diseases born of skin disorders. They may experience eczema <note>original: "vicharchika"</note>, illnesses related to bile <term>pitta: one of the three bodily humors in Ayurveda associated with heat and metabolism</term>, and jaundice. There is a risk of death or wasting away of the body due to the wrath of kings, fire, or thieves. || 25 ||

Even when Mercury <note>original: "Shashankasuno"; literally 'the son of the Moon'</note> is situated in the twelfth house, there is a fear of bodily deformity, hatred toward one's wife and kinsmen, and anger bestowed by the sovereign. One may face sudden fear of death and negligence. || 26 ||

When Mercury is situated in the house of the spouse <note>the 7th house</note>, during the fruition of its period, one gains children, a wife, and wealth. There is the enjoyment of knowledge, clean garments, the acquisition of a second name <note>likely a title or honorific</note>, and friendship with the king. || 27 ||

When Mercury is situated in the house of fortune <note>the 9th house</note>, the person gains an increase in luck, a wife, children, and wealth. The person shall attain the merit of bathing in holy waters <note>original: "tirtha-abhishekam"</note>, the chanting of prayers, fire sacrifices, charity, and the performance of Vedic rituals. || 28 ||

When Mercury is situated in the house of action <note>the 10th house</note>, during the fruition of its period, one attains a status equal to a king. One finds happiness, composes prose and poetry marked with one's own name, gains a second name, and acquires a wife, children, and wealth. || 29 ||

One performs the worship of gods and Brahmins <note>original: "mahiruhanam"; literally 'gods of the earth'</note>, gains sovereignty, and leadership over the people. At this time, one follows the path of poetry and undergoes initiation for sacrifices, especially alongside one's kinsmen. || 30 ||

During the period of Mercury situated in the eleventh house <note>original: "upantya-rashi"; the house of gains</note>, wealth comes in many ways: through charity, through honors from the king, or through agriculture and commercial considerations. || 31 ||

When Mercury is joined with its sign of exaltation <note>original: "ucchamsha"</note>, during its specific period, one obtains children and ornaments. There is mental delight, a beauty like that of the god of love <note>original: "Madana"</note>, enthusiasm, courage, and ceremonial baths. || 32 ||

Mercury joined with its sign of debilitation <note>original: "nichansha"</note> causes one to live through lowly occupations. During its period, it brings about servitude and abandonment. || 33 ||

In the period of Mercury, a person first obtains wealth, grain, and prosperity. At the end of the period, there is opposition from kinsmen, but in the middle of the period, one receives honors from the ruler. || 34 ||

In the period of Mercury when it is associated with the Sun, one experiences various calamities and mental grief. There is opposition from one's own kinsmen and the king, or fear of censure, and diseases of the eyes and ears. || 35 ||

When Mercury is endowed with <term>Sthana-virya</term><note>Positional strength based on its placement in specific zodiac signs</note>, its period bestows fame and kingdom. It grants mental courage, enthusiasm, and the auspicious initiation into sacrifices. || 36 ||

If Mercury is devoid of that positional strength, there is great fear regarding one's place of residence, wife, and children. One lives in a foreign land, suffers grief, and undergoes various types of humiliation. || 37 ||

When Mercury is possessed of <term>Dig-virya</term><note>Directional strength; for Mercury, this is the East or the 1st House</note>, the person becomes wealthy and wise, gaining riches from the ends of the earth. They enjoy friendship with vassal kings and the pleasure of perfumes and flower garlands. || 38 ||

In the period of Mercury endowed with <term>Kala-virya</term><note>Temporal strength based on the time of birth (day/night)</note>, one attains physical comfort but also separation due to quarrels. One receives honors from wife, children, and the king, and the body becomes purified by the waters of the Ganges. || 39 ||

In the period of Mercury endowed with <term>Nisarga-virya</term><note>Innate or natural strength</note>, auspicious deeds occur naturally. However, there may be disputes over learning, opposition from kinsmen, or separation from the mother or her relatives. || 40 ||

When Mercury is possessed of <term>Vakra-chesta</term><note>Strength derived from retrograde motion</note>, one enjoys fortune, a wife, children, and wealth. Likewise, one performs the reading of the Puranas, gives charities, and bathes in the ocean. || 41 ||

When Mercury is joined with <term>Drik-bala</term><note>Aspect strength; the power gained when being looked at by auspicious planets</note>, it creates a gentle disposition toward all beings. It brings the play of love along with the possession of a kingdom and good fortune. || 42 ||

In the period of Mercury placed in a <term>Krura-shashtyansha</term><note>A "cruel" 1/60th division of a sign</note>, there is great fear. If it is also devoid of the aspect or association of auspicious planets, there will be fear from thieves, fire, and kings. || 43 ||

When Mercury is in a <term>Mridu-ansha</term><note>A "soft" or "mild" division of a sign</note> and similar positions, there is gain of kingdom and great happiness. One shows gentleness toward all beings and gains wealth through agriculture, children, and riches. || 44 ||

If Mercury is situated in a <term>Vaisheshika-ansha</term><note>A specific high-quality division in the ten-fold varga system</note>, one is especially honored by kings. One enjoys fragrant clothes and garlands, and gains access to secret assemblies of the learned. || 45 ||

When the son of the Moon <note>A poetic name for Mercury</note> is joined with a <term>Krura-dreshkana</term><note>A "cruel" 1/3rd division of a sign, often associated with violence</note>, then there is fear of thieves, fire, and the king, as well as loss of position and great terror. || 46 ||

If Mercury is located in its sign of exaltation <note>the zodiac sign where a planet is strongest; for Mercury, this is Virgo</note> but is positioned in a debilitated subdivision <note>original: "nichabhaga"; referring to the Navamsha or ninth-part division where the planet's strength is diminished</note>, it will instantly destroy kingdom, happiness, and great fame. || 47 ||

Even if the son of the Moon <note>Mercury</note> is in its sign of debilitation <note>Pisces</note>, if it is joined with its exalted subdivision, it gives inauspicious results at the beginning but provides auspicious results at the end of its period. || 48 ||

**Thus ends the period of Mercury. Thus ends the fourteenth chapter of the Sarvartha Chintamani.** || ||

### Now begins the Period of Jupiter

In the period of Jupiter, when he is in his highest exaltation <note>Cancer</note>, the person attains a kingdom, great happiness, and fame. They experience mental delight, possess groups of elephants and horses <note>symbols of high status and military power</note>, receive a royal consecration, and gain leadership over their own clan. || 1 ||

In the period of Jupiter, even if located in Cancer <note>his exaltation sign</note>, there may be a rise in fortune through the honor of a king, or travel to foreign lands and great authority; however, the person may also find their body distressed by various sufferings. || 2 ||

When the period of the Teacher of the Gods <note>Jupiter</note> is "ascending" <note>term: <term>Arohini</term> (a planet moving from its sign of debilitation toward its sign of exaltation)</note>, it brings greatness and provides wealth and land. The person gains through musical activities, women, and children, is honored by kings, and attains fame and majesty through their own valor. || 3 ||

During the ascending period of Jupiter, the person becomes a lord or a ruler of a district. They obtain wealth from priests and kings, and are intelligent, radiant, and humble in their knowledge. || 4 ||

The "descending" period <note>term: <term>Avaroha</term> (a planet moving from its sign of exaltation toward its sign of debilitation)</note> of the one worshiped by Indra <note>Jupiter</note> produces happiness only once, followed by destruction. It brings a flash of fame and special brilliance, and the person attains the status of a ruler only briefly. || 5 ||

In the period of Jupiter when he occupies his most debilitated subdivision, the person's collection of houses is broken down. They experience mutual heart-felt enmity, the destruction of their agriculture, and face the ultimate death. || 6 ||

In the period of Jupiter when he resides in his "Root Trine" <note>term: <term>Mulatrikona</term> (a specific favorable placement in a sign, for Jupiter this is Sagittarius)</note>, there is special happiness regarding kingdom, wealth, land, children, and spouse. The person rides in vehicles, gains wealth through their own strength, and their footstool is honored by people during sacrifices and rituals. || 7 ||

In the period of Jupiter when he has gone to his own house <note>Sagittarius or Pisces</note>, there is wealth from the king, land, grain, happiness, and fine clothing.

During the major period of Jupiter <note>original: "Jiva-dasha"</note> when it is associated with the Sun <note>original: "Arka-ga"</note>, a person may suddenly suffer from fever and become physically weak. They may experience diseases in the upper parts of the body, develop a difficult temperament, and face the ruin of their domestic life. || 29 ||

At the beginning of Jupiter's major period, one receives honor from the king <note>or high authorities</note> and great happiness. In the middle of the period, there is the gain of a wife, children, and wealth. However, at the end of the period, one should predict difficulties. || 30 ||

When Jupiter is situated in the second house <note>the house of wealth</note> during its ripening period <note>Vipaka/Dasha</note>, there is an influx of wealth and honor from the sovereign. One participates in royal assemblies marked by scholarly debates, performs acts of charity for all, and achieves victory and happiness. || 31 ||

One receives great honors from the king and gains land through brothers. Wealth, cattle, and land may be gifted by foreign women <note>or women from other families</note>. One acquires fine food, clothing, ornaments, perfumes, and garlands, and experiences the benefits of others' service while gaining wisdom and valor. || 32 ||

During the period of Jupiter situated in the third house, there is happiness and wealth for one's brothers. One receives wealth given by the king, along with comforts such as perfumes, garlands, and fine garments. || 33 ||

In the major period of Jupiter situated in the sixth house <note>the house of enemies/illness</note> from the Ascendant, there is freedom from disease and the gain of children and a wife. While this is the case at the beginning, by the end of the period, there is fear from thieves regarding one's wife and wealth, as well as the onset of illness. || 34 ||

Jupiter situated in the eighth house <note>the house of death/transformation</note> brings happiness but also causes the loss of one's kinsmen. It leads to a fall from one's position and travel to foreign lands, though at the very end, it brings honor from women, the king, and sons. || 35 ||

When the major period of Jupiter in the eleventh house <note>the house of gains</note> arrives, one attains the gains of a kingdom <note>or high status</note>. One acquires much wealth, a wife, and children, yet may also face opposition from the king and enmity with one's own relatives. || 36 ||

When the major period of Jupiter in the twelfth house <note>the house of loss/expenditure</note> arrives, one acquires vehicles and the like, but also travels to foreign lands and is overcome by various afflictions. || 37 ||

During the ripening of a Jupiter endowed with "positional strength" <note>Sthana-bala</note>, one acquires land, wealth, a wife, and children, as well as elephants, horses, gold, and multicolored garments and ornaments. When the "Lord of the Gods" (Jupiter) is endowed with "directional strength" <note>Dig-bala</note>, one becomes famous in the world; and when Jupiter possesses "temporal strength" <note>Kala-bala</note>, one receives honors from the king's wife.

In the period of Saturn when aspected <note>glanced at by the influence of</note> by malefic planets, there is the destruction of servants, wealth, wife, children, and siblings. One faces public scandal, bad food, and receives foul-smelling garlands. || 17 ||

In the period of Saturn when aspected by benefic planets, one initially gains a wife, children, servants, and wealth. Later, however, one faces great hardships and the destruction of cattle, land, trade, and agriculture. || 18 ||

In the period of Saturn when placed in a "center" <term>kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a birth chart</term>, there is suffering from quarrels and fatigue. The death of children, friends, wealth, wife, and kinsmen is certain. || 19 ||

During the period of Saturn situated in the **fourth house**, there is the destruction of the mother's side of the family, the burning of the house, loss of status, trouble from thieves, and oppression by the ruler. || 21 ||

Even when Saturn is in the **seventh house** <note>the house of partnerships and marriage</note>, its period brings trouble from enemies, urinary disorders <term>Mutrakricchra</term> <note>painful or difficult urination</note>, great hatred, or even death on account of a woman. || 22 ||

During the period of Saturn in the **ninth house**, one suffers the loss of parents and teachers; one travels abroad, and one's own family and caste face ruin. || 29 ||

During the period of Saturn in the **eleventh house** <note>the house of gains</note>, one attains various types of wealth, happiness, and honors, the well-being of children, wife, and servants, mental delight, and wealth acquired from agriculture. || 30 ||

<margin>Chapter 16 Page 80</margin>### Now, the Results of the Rahu Period

For Rahu, Taurus is the sign of exaltation, while for Ketu <note>the South Node</note>, Scorpio is considered the sign of exaltation. Aquarius is the primary root-triangle <term>Mulatrikona: a sign where a planet is particularly strong, second only to exaltation</term>, and Aries is said to be its friendly sign. || 1 || The seventh sign from this <note>Leo</note> is the primary root-triangle for Ketu. If Rahu is placed in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth houses <note>the "Dusthanas" or difficult houses in astrology</note>, it will cause suffering during its period. || 2 ||

When Rahu <note>original: "Saimhikeya," a name for Rahu meaning "son of Simhika"</note> is in its sign of exaltation, it brings happiness during its ripening <term>Paka: the period when a planet's influence bears fruit</term>. It grants kingdom, the acquisition of friends, and an increase in wealth and grain. || 3 || If Rahu is in its sign of debilitation during its period, it gives fear from thieves, fire, and kings. The son of Simhika <note>Rahu</note> causes fear from hanging and poison. || 4 ||

Upon the arrival of the Rahu period, there is oppression from kings and thieves, travel to foreign lands, great sorrow, and certain fear from living in the forest. || 5 || During the period of Rahu located in the first house <term>Lagna: the Ascendant or rising sign</term>, one suffers from a loss of intelligence and harm from poison, fire, or weapons. One experiences the loss of kinsmen, great sorrow, and defeat in battle. || 6 ||

In the period of Rahu located in the second house <note>the house of wealth</note>, it specifically takes away kingdom and wealth. It leads to poor food, service to a wicked king, mental agitation, falsehood, and anger. || 7 || During the time of Rahu in the third house, there is happiness for sons, wealth, wives, and brothers. There is growth in agriculture, authority, foreign travel, and honor from the protector of men <note>the King</note>. || 8 ||

In the period of Rahu in the fourth house, there is the loss of the mother or her suffering. There is loss of lands and wealth, the anger of the king, the fall of the wife, and many sorrows. || 9 || There is distress from thieves, fire, and imprisonment, as well as mental agitation and suffering from disease for the wife and children. Four—

If Rahu is in a sign owned by a gentle planet <note>benefic</note>, such results occur; if in a sign owned by a cruel planet <note>malefic</note>, it is indeed so. All the results mentioned are such if in a gentle sign; otherwise, they are different. || 17 ||

If Rahu has gone to a malefic field <note>a sign ruled by a cruel planet</note>, is in the house of action <note>10th House</note>, and is joined with malefic planets, then at that time one is cursed and suffers pain regarding children, wife, and fire. || 18 ||

When Rahu has gone to the sign of gains <note>the 11th House</note>, in its ripening there is honor from the king. There is the acquisition of wealth, the gaining of a wife, and prosperity in houses, fields, and so on. || 19 ||

In the period of Rahu gone to the house of expenditure <note>the 12th House</note>, it causes the loss of one's country and mental affliction. It causes separation from wife and children, and the destruction of agriculture, cattle, wealth, and grain. || 20 ||

During the ripening of the period <term>Dasha<note>A major planetary period in Vedic astrology that governs a specific span of a person's life.</note></term> of **Rahu** <note>The North Node of the Moon, often depicted as a shadow planet or dragon's head.</note> when placed in Cancer, Taurus, or Aries, the individual attains wealth. They experience the joy of knowledge, honor from the king, and happiness from their spouse, servants, and children. || 21 ||

During the ripening of the period of **Rahu** when placed in Virgo, Pisces, or Sagittarius, one gains children and a spouse. They achieve lordship over a territory and possess human-drawn vehicles <note>original: "naravahanam"; likely referring to palanquins or high-status transport</note>, but at the very end of the period, everything is destroyed. || 22 ||

During the period of the "Lord of Serpents" <note>original: "Phanindra," an epithet for Rahu</note> when associated with malefic signs, there is emaciation of the body and the destruction of one's own lineage. There is fear from the king, fear of enemies through deception, and ailments such as urinary disorders <note>original: "prameha"</note>, cough, consumption <note>tuberculosis</note>, and painful urination. || 23 ||

**Rahu**, when combined with the gaze <term>Drishti<note>An astrological aspect where one planet 'looks' at or influences another.</note></term> of a benefic planet, brings success in actions. It ensures honor from the king and the acquisition of wealth, though the death of kinsmen is certain. || 24 ||

**Rahu**, when combined with the gaze of a malefic planet, causes the destruction of one's work. It brings about the failure of industry, bodily pain, and suffering caused by thieves, fire, or the king. || 25 ||

**Rahu**, when joined with an exalted planet, brings the gain of a kingdom. One acquires a wife, sons, wealth, property, fine clothes, jewelry, and fragrant ointments. || 26 ||

**Rahu**, when joined with a debilitated planet, leads to a livelihood through lowly means. At that time, one receives poor food and suffers from a wicked spouse and a wicked son. || 27 ||

At the beginning of the period, one encounters sorrow; in the middle of the period, happiness and fame; and at the end of the period, the loss of one's position and the loss of teachers and children. || 28 ||

**Thus ends the period of Rahu.**

### Now, the results of the period of Ketu:

The destruction of wife and children, fear of the king, and great hardship; the acquisition of knowledge, kinsmen, and wealth, yet remaining devoid of friends; fear from disease, fire, and enemies. Falling while riding a vehicle, fear from poison, water, or weapons, exile from one's country to another, a taste for quarreling, or fear regarding trade and commodities. || 1 ||

Upon the arrival of the period of **Ketu** <note>The South Node of the Moon, depicted as a headless body or dragon's tail.</note>, there is the destruction of spouse and children. One suffers the king's anger, mental agony, and the destruction of agriculture by thieves or fire. || 2 ||

The period of **Ketu** situated in a <term>Kendra<note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a birth chart, considered the 'pillars' of a horoscope.</note></term> makes actions fruitless. For the sake of the kingdom and wealth—

If Ketu is placed in the second house <note>original: "dhanarashi," the house of wealth</note>, its period causes the loss of wealth, harshness of speech, mental distress, consumption of poor quality food, and mental illness. || 5 ||

If Ketu is placed in the third house, its period brings great happiness <note>This is a common paradox in astrology where Ketu in the 3rd can grant worldly success but internal strife.</note>, yet the mind suffers from confusion and there is great enmity with one's brothers. || 6 ||

If Ketu is placed in the fourth house, its period causes a loss of happiness; the person suffers the loss of wife, children, and home, and a depletion of grain and resources. || 7 ||

During the period of Ketu situated in the fifth house, there is the loss of children, significant mental confusion, the wrath of the king <note>In a modern context, this refers to legal troubles or issues with government authorities.</note>, and loss of wealth. || 8 ||

During the period of Ketu situated in the sixth house <note>original: "arigata," the house of enemies</note>, there is great fear; there will be fear of thieves, fire, and poison, and one encounters extreme distress. || 9 ||

In the period of Ketu joined with the seventh house <note>original: "kalatrarashi," the house of the spouse</note>, there is great fear, the loss of wife, children, and wealth, as well as urinary diseases and mental illness. || 10 ||

During the period of Ketu joined with the eighth house, there is great fear, the death of the father, and the person is afflicted with asthma, cough, dysentery, and consumption <note>tuberculosis or general wasting of the body</note>. || 11 ||

In the ripening of the period of Ketu in the ninth house, there is misfortune for the father or misfortune and grief for the Guru <note>teacher or spiritual guide</note>, and the destruction of auspicious deeds. || 12 ||

Upon reaching the period of Ketu in the tenth house <note>original: "karmastha," the house of profession and action</note>, one may attain some happiness, yet there is loss of honor, mental dullness, infamy, and mental illness. || 13 ||

Upon reaching the period of Ketu in the eleventh house <note>original: "labhastha," the house of gains</note>, the period bestows happiness, joy from brothers and kin, and the increase of sacrifices <note>religious rituals</note> and wife. || 14 ||

Upon reaching the period of Ketu in the twelfth house <note>original: "rihphastha," the house of loss and liberation</note>, the period becomes most difficult; there is displacement from one's position, foreign travel, oppression by the king, and the loss of eyesight. || 15 ||

At the beginning of the period, one attains happiness, but in the middle of the period, great fear—

<margin>S. Chi. 82</margin> ...At the end of the <term>Dasha</term><note>The major planetary period in Vedic astrology</note>, there is fear of the king <note>or government authorities</note> and physical lethargy. || 16 ||
<margin>Ch. 16</margin> If <term>Ketu</term><note>The South Node of the Moon, often depicted as a shadow planet</note> is associated with the aspect of a benefic planet, it brings happiness, acquisition of a kingdom, peace in the home, and very firm royal honors. || 17 || If Ketu is associated with the lord of a malefic house, it causes suffering, fever, dysentery, urinary diseases, skin disorders, and oppression from the king. || 18 ||

**Thus ends the period of Ketu.**

### Now, the Results of the Sub-periods

A person becomes radiant, very happy, with stable wealth, and receives riches from the king. If the planet is strong in its own <term>Navamsha</term><note>A one-ninth divisional chart used to determine a planet's true strength</note>, it makes the person wealthy and famous. || 1 || If associated with the results of benefic aspects, it makes the person famous and wealthy, charming in their efforts, pure, handsome, and very gentle. || 2 ||

When the lords of the major period and sub-period are in a <term>Shashtashtaka</term><note>A 6th-8th house relationship, considered highly unfavorable in astrology</note> position from each other, there is fear of the king and opposition from servants. There is conflict with one's wife, loss of children and spouse, and mental distress caused by thieves, fire, or kinsmen. || 3 ||

During the sub-period of a planet situated in the twelfth house from the lord of the major period, there is displacement from one's position and opposition from kinsmen. One travels to foreign lands, faces conflict with relatives, and suffers from diseases of the feet, eyes, or heart. || 4 ||

During the sub-period of a planet conjoined with the lord of the major period, there is destruction of wealth, agriculture, and the welfare of wife, children, and servants. There is failure in industry, great distress from relatives, and sudden accusations. || 5 ||

During the sub-period of a planet situated in the second house from the lord of the major period, one obtains soft food, drinks, garments, perfumes, and ministerial status. One performs acts of charity, enjoys friendship with relatives, and experiences mental delight through wife, children, and kinsmen. || 6 ||
<margin>82</margin> During the sub-period of a planet situated in the third house <note>the house of siblings</note> from the lord of the major period, one receives favors and friendship from the king. One acquires fragrant garlands, clothing, and ornaments, and enjoys the happiness of food and nourishment arising from friends. || 7 ||

During the sub-period of a planet situated in the fourth house <note>the house of the home and mother</note> from the lord of the major period, there is the acquisition of a wife, children, wealth, and a house, as well as religious pilgrimages. One obtains sweet food, drinks, clothing, and ornaments...

...suffering and the destruction of kingdom, wealth, and home. || 1 ||
Such is the fruit of the Lord of Day <note>original: "Dinesha," a title for the Sun</note> when the planets are in unfavorable transit positions. When a planet is in a favorable transit <term>Gochara: the current movement of planets across the zodiac relative to one's birth chart</term>, the fruit is happiness throughout the entire planetary period <term>Paka: the ripening or duration of a planet's influence, often synonymous with Dasha</term>. || 2 ||

-> **Definition of Favorable Transit** <-

A planet is considered to be in a favorable transit <note>original: "Gochara-stha"</note> when it is situated in its own sign, its sign of exaltation, or its "root-trine" <term>Mulatrikona: a specific favorable area within a zodiac sign where a planet's power is concentrated</term>, provided it is not in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth houses, is not combust <note>hidden by the Sun's glare</note>, and is in a friend's sign. || 3 ||

A planet is considered to be in an unfavorable transit <note>original: "Agochara"</note> if it is combust, in its sign of debilitation, away from its own sign or root-trine, or situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth houses <note>these are the "Dusthanas" or difficult houses in Indian astrology</note>. || 4 ||

During the major period <term>Dasha: a primary time-block in a person's life ruled by a specific planet</term> of the Lord of Day <note>the Sun</note> when it is located in the first house <note>the Ascendant or "Lagna"</note>:
In the sub-periods <term>Bhukti: a secondary time-cycle within a Dasha</term> of Jupiter and Venus, or of the Moon and Mercury, one gains agriculture, cattle, children, a spouse, and land. || 5 ||

During the major period of the Lord of Day located in the second house:
In the sub-period of a malefic planet <note>such as Mars or Saturn</note>, there is loss of wealth, harshness of speech, mental grief, eye disease, and great fear. || 6 ||
In the sub-period of a benefic planet during the Sun's ripening in the second house, there is great happiness, acquisition of knowledge, favor from the king <note>or government</note>, clothing, vehicles, and ornaments. || 7 ||

When the Sun is in the third house:
During a malefic sub-period, if the planet is in a favorable transit, there is great happiness; otherwise, one should predict malefic results. || 8 ||
During the Sun's ripening in that same house, in a benefic sub-period, there is great happiness, courage, wealth, and—despite some distress regarding children—victory in battle. || 9 ||

During the major period of the Lord of Day located in the fourth house:
In the sub-period of malefics, there is the loss of the mother, mental grief, and affliction from thieves, fire, or the king. || 10 ||
Even with the Sun in the fourth house, during a benefic sub-period, there is great happiness, kingdom, wealth, children, a spouse, clothing, garlands, and fragrant ointments. || 11 ||

During the major period of the Sun in the fifth house:
In the sub-periods of Saturn, Mars, Rahu <note>original: "Shikhi," the North Node of the Moon</note>, or Ketu <note>original: "Bhogi," the South Node</note>, there is distress regarding children and affliction from thieves, kings, or fire. || 12 ||
In the sub-periods of benefic planets for the Sun situated in the fifth house:
During the ripening, there is distress regarding children <note>a repeating theme for the 5th house</note>, but also kingdom, vehicles, and ornaments. || 13 ||

# The Results of the Sub-Periods during the Major Period of the Moon

### The Sub-period of Mars (Dharasunu)

Thus ends the general description of the Moon's major period. Now follows the results of the sub-period <term>Antardasha|A secondary planetary period that operates within a major cycle (Mahadasha)</term> of Mars <note>original: "Dharasunu," literally "Son of the Earth," a common synonym for the planet Mars</note> when positioned in various houses:

**Mars in the First House (Ascendant)**
When Mars is situated in the First House <term>Lagna|The Ascendant or the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the time of birth</term>, during its maturation <note>original: "paripake," referring to the time the planetary influence bears fruit</note>, one may suffer from wounds or injuries. If this occurs during an inauspicious sub-division <note>original: "papa-bhukti," a minor period ruled by a malefic planet</note>, there will be great distress and significant fear arising from indigestion and similar ailments. **[1]**

If it occurs during an auspicious sub-division, one receives affection from the king <note>In a modern context, this implies favor from the government or employers</note>, well-being for one's brothers, and general happiness. During such a period of Mars, one also acquires landed property and vehicles. **[2]**

**Mars in the Second House**
When Mars is in the Second House <note>The house associated with wealth and speech</note> and an auspicious sub-division occurs, there is happiness regarding brothers, mental enthusiasm, and the acquisition of knowledge, vehicles, and ornaments. **[3]**

However, during the general maturation of Mars in the Second House, there can also be an auspicious "theft" <note>original: "shubha hriti," likely implying a redistribution of resources</note>, the loss of previously earned wealth, and suffering from the king's anger, fevers, or fire. **[4]**

**Mars in the Third House**
When Mars is in the Third House <note>The house of courage and siblings</note> during an inauspicious sub-division, the individual suffers from mental instability and the loss of brothers. **[5]**

If the sub-division is gentle <note>original: "saumya-hriti," a period ruled by a benefic planet like Venus or Jupiter</note> while Mars is in the Third House, one enjoys good food and clothing, success in agriculture, and the acquisition of ornaments and vehicles. **[6]**

**Mars in the Fourth House (Hibuka)**
When Mars is in the Fourth House <note>original: "Hibuka," a Greek-derived term (hypogeion) used in Indian astrology for the 4th house, relating to home and mother</note> during a cruel sub-division, there is great fear, the destruction of home and fields, and affliction from the king, thieves, or fire. **[7]**

If the sub-division is gentle, one attains land, clothing, and happiness, as well as livestock, vehicles, and ornaments. **[8]**

**Mars in the Fifth House**
When Mars is in the Fifth House <note>The house of children and intelligence</note> during an inauspicious sub-division, there is the destruction of agriculture, cattle, wealth, grain, and even loss regarding sons and wife. **[9]**

Under a gentle sub-division for Mars <note>original: "Kuja," another name for Mars</note> in this position, one should predict auspicious things: honor from the king, though perhaps some anxiety regarding a son, and the attainment of sacred mantras. **[10]**

**Mars in the Sixth House**
When Mars is in the Sixth House <note>The house of enemies, debt, and disease</note> during an inauspicious sub-division, one should point out hardships: trouble from thieves, fire, and the king, as well as skin eruptions, wasting diseases, and urinary ailments. **[11]**

Under a gentle sub-division, one gains the friendship of the king, but there may be the loss of kinsmen and mental grief, followed later by happiness. **[12]**

**Mars in the Seventh House (Kalatra)**
When Mars is in the Seventh House <note>original: "Kalatra," the house of marriage and partnerships</note> during an inauspicious sub-division, there is fear regarding the wife, sons, and the king...

<term>Dasha (period)</term>: A system in Indian astrology where specific time blocks of a person's life are ruled by a particular planet.
<term>Bhukti (sub-period)</term>: A smaller division within a Dasha, where a second planet influences the primary ruler.
<term>Rahu (The Serpent)</term>: A "shadow planet" in Vedic astrology representing the North Node of the Moon, often associated with sudden changes and karmic retribution.

It specifically warns of the transition from initial success to eventual hardship or "fear of the king" at the end of these cycles.</summary>

Hatred from relatives, a troubled mind, and poverty in speech <note>Likely referring to a loss of eloquence or being forced to speak submissively</note>. One suffers from bad food, evil deeds, and a miserable state of servitude. || 21 ||

At the end of the sub-period, one should predict a change of place and sudden quarrels. || 8 || During the period of Ketu, if it is placed in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth houses <note>known as the 'Dusthanas' or difficult houses</note>, the sub-period is unfavorable. It causes death, travel to a foreign land, or a fall from one's position. || 9 || Afflictions such as urinary diseases, <term>Gulma</term> <note>chronic enlargement of the spleen or abdominal tumors</note>, and harassment from the king, thieves, or fire. Such are the fruits at the beginning, though at the end, there is some slight increase in happiness. || 10 || During the sub-period of gentle <note>benefic</note> planets, there is an increase in wives and sons. Acquisition of grain, clothing, ornaments, excellent gems, and gold. || 11 || Deception, yet also valor; similarly, a fall from a position of value or price. Enmity with one's own kinsmen, and ailments of the head, eyes, or rectum. || 12 || During the ripening of Ketu when associated with the third or eleventh houses, there is great happiness. In an auspicious sub-period, there is favor from the king and various wonderful clothes and ornaments. || 13 || Vehicles, gain of land, and the enjoyment of perfumes, garlands, and ointments. The arrival of wealth from afar and being honored by one's own kinsmen. || 14 || In a malefic sub-period, the person may perform sinful deeds. There is the creation of obstacles in all matters, and a life abandoned by relatives. || 15 || Serving others and wearing poor clothing—such is the fruit at the beginning of the sub-period.

(16) Even if Ketu is placed in the house of wealth <note>the second house</note>, during its ripening <term>Paripaka: the period when a planet's influence reaches its peak</term>, it may bring unfavorable results.

One performs acts of charity for all and receives food, clothing, and ornaments. (19) Such are the fruits at the beginning of the sub-period; at the end, there is some expenditure of wealth.
Harshness of speech, mental agitation, or the failure of one's undertakings. (20) **Thus ends the sub-period of Ketu. Now begins the sub-period of Venus.**

When the sub-period of Venus (Shukra) occurs while it is situated in a quadrant <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a horoscope, considered pillars of strength</term> and associated with benefics, one attains a kingdom, royal honors, vehicles, clothing, and ornaments. (1)
Enthusiasm, fame, prosperity, and the wealth of wife, children, and riches. An increase in fortune, mental courage, and authority at the gates of the royal palace. (2)
If such a bright Venus <note>original: "vacchasya", likely referring to the pure or bright planet</note> is in a malefic sub-period, there is loss of wealth, poor food, poor clothing, and the destruction of good deeds. (3)

When Venus is situated in a trine <term>Trikona: the 1st, 5th, or 9th houses, associated with luck and merit</term>, during a favorable sub-period, there are auspicious activities. Devotion to the gods and the learned <note>original: "bhusura", literally 'gods of the earth' or Brahmins</note>, and the flourishing of children and wife. During a favorable sub-period, one gains great fame, honors from the king <note>original: "rajasammanam"; refers to recognition from government or high authorities</note>, acquisition of wealth, and the prosperity of children, wife, and riches. || 9 || At the beginning, one acquires garments, vehicles, and ornaments, but at the end, there is mental distress, hatred from kinsmen, the loss of a teacher, and the destruction of one's own family lineage. || 10 || During the sub-periods of auspicious planets, there is bodily health and great happiness, food provided by others, the acquisition of silk garments, and ornaments of perfumes and garlands. || 11 || Such are the fruits at the beginning of the liberation <note>original: "muktyadau"; Whichever <term>Nakshatra</term> <note>Lunar mansion or star constellation</note> is found to be in an increasing or strengthened state at the time of birth, it is certain that the person will attain wealth, long life, and health. || 1 ||

The same should be said regarding the <term>Tithis</term> <note>Lunar days</note> and other factors; if they are in a state of decay or weakness, then a decline in fortune occurs. A Lunar day is said to have a single measure of influence, while a Star constellation is ten times more powerful. || 2 ||

The <term>Lagna</term> <note>The Ascendant or the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note> is said to be a hundred thousand times more powerful; the overall results of a life are determined by the combination of these factors. If all the "malefic" planets <note>planets considered to have a harsh influence, such as Mars or Saturn</note> are situated in the <term>Kendras</term> <note>The "Angular" houses of a birth chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note> at the time of birth, they yield fruitless or negative results. || 3 ||

They cause poverty, many sorrows, and ailments such as respiratory diseases, wasting, disorders of the spleen, and abdominal or rectal pains. || 4 ||

When a <term>Papagraha</term> <note>Malefic planet</note> is in the tenth house, in its sign of extreme debilitation, in retrograde motion, or joined by other malefic planets, the great sages of many scriptures surely declare the destruction of the spouse. || 5 ||

The person will be sorrowful, foolish, hated by people, blind in one eye, lame, poor, and without honor. If all malefic planets are in the Angular houses, the person will have a short life, be a hater of the learned <note>original: "brahmadveṣī" - one who hates Brahmins or divine knowledge</note>, and possess a bad reputation. || 6 ||

**Shankaracharya** <note>A famous philosopher, here cited as an authority on astrological combinations</note> says: If all malefic planets are situated in the first, tenth, seventh, or fourth houses at the time of birth, they indicate a short lifespan, especially if one of them is the lord of the Ascendant. || 7 ||

Even so, the sages declare that the measure of the results of such a combination will be of that specific kind. Even in a "King-making" combination <note>Yoga</note>, if planets are in their signs of debilitation, the result is a life of sorrow and exhaustion. || 8 ||

In whose birth such a position exists, there is suffering and the death of parents during childhood. The filling of the stomach occurs only through begging for food, and the person may suffer from physical disabilities. || 9 ||

However, even if a person is born with planets in their signs of debilitation, if a "benefic" planet <note>such as Jupiter or Venus</note> is situated in the Angular or Trinal houses <note>1st, 4th, 7th, 10th or 1st, 5th, 9th houses</note>, they declare that the <term>Rajayoga</term> <note>A "Royal Union" or combination indicating high status and success</note> will become fruitful. || 10 ||

If the Ascendant is occupied by a benefic portion, is aspected by its own exalted planet, and is seen by Jupiter or the lord of the house of wealth, then even if planets are in their debilitated portions—

Even if one is born in a humble condition, through the application of these planetary combinations, they shall attain lordship over the earth. || 11 || Thus it was spoken in the *Chintamani* <note>The "Thought-Gem," a reference to the title of the treatise</note> by the wise Venkatesha, regarding the fruits arising from the debility of planetary portions and the formation of Royal Unions <note>term: Rajayoga (combinations indicating power and success)</note>. || 12 ||

### On the Decans
<note>term: Drekkana (a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign, often personified or associated with specific imagery)</note>

Now, the Decans: The second decan of Aries is a Bird-Decan. The second decan of Gemini is a Bird-Decan. Now, the second of Cancer; the third of Cancer is also a Serpent-Decan. The first of Leo is a Bird-Decan. The first and second of Scorpio are Serpent-Decans. The third of Scorpio is a Serpent. Now, the first of Capricorn is a Fetter-Decan <note>original: "Nigada," representing bondage or restriction</note>. The third of Pisces is a Serpent-Decan.

The Sun, Mars, and Saturn are "dry" planets. The Moon and Venus are "watery." Mercury and Jupiter are to be known as watery only when they occupy watery signs. || 1 || Aquarius, Cancer, Pisces, Capricorn, Scorpio, and Libra are declared to be watery signs; the remaining signs are waterless.

**Thus ends the *Sarvartha Chintamani* <note>The "Thought-Gem of All Purposes"</note>.**

The Sun, Mercury, Rahu <note>original: "Saimhikeya," the son of Simhika</note>, Jupiter, Ketu, the Moon, Saturn, Venus, and Mars: these planets, according to the strength of the stars <note>term: Tarabala (the strength derived from the moon's transit through specific asterisms)</note>, daily bring about heat, luster, loss, courage, destruction, loss of fame, joy, and death, respectively, as they transit. || 1 ||

### On Obstruction
The author now describes the obstructing nature of planets based on their positions relative to one another:

For the Moveable, Fixed, and Dual signs <note>The three categories of zodiac signs</note>, the lords of the 11th, 9th, and 7th houses respectively are the "Obstructors" <note>term: Badhaka (planets that create hurdles for specific rising signs)</note>. Furthermore, the lords of the signs occupied by the Sun or Mandi <note>A sensitive mathematical point in a chart associated with Saturn</note> are planets that cause extreme obstruction. || 2 ||

### On Significators
The Sun (1), Jupiter (2), Mars (3), the Moon and Mercury (4), Jupiter (5), Saturn (6), Venus (7), Saturn (8), the Sun and Jupiter (9), Jupiter, the Sun, and Saturn (10), Jupiter (11), and Saturn (12) are the Significators <note>term: Karaka (planets that act as "doers" or indicators for specific life departments)</note> counted from the Ascendant. || 3 ||

### || Now, the special significations of the planets are described ||

<margin>Sarvartha Chintamani 92</margin> <margin>Chapter 16, 92</margin>
The **Sun** is the significator <note>Sanskrit: 'karaka', the planet responsible for bringing a certain quality into a person's life</note> of the father, majesty, health, purity of mind, taste, and the dawn of knowledge. || 1 || The **Moon** is the significator of the white fly-whisk <note>a symbol of royalty and status</note>, fame, mercy, delight, luster, facial beauty, the mother, and the contentment of the mind. || 2 || **Mars** is the significator of valor, victory, renown, courage in battle, leadership of the army, the power of punishment, and weapons such as the sword, battle-axe, spear, hatchet, the 'shataghni' <note>literally 'hundred-killer', an ancient projectile weapon or cannon</note>, the 'bhindipala' <note>a type of sling or javelin</note>, and skill in archery. He also governs fortitude, gravity, desire, anger, the increase of enemies, loss of income, restraint, majesty, infamy, independence, the creator, and the earth. || 3 || **Mercury** is the significator of progeny, peace, humility, devotion, intellect, the maternal uncle, kinsmen, relatives, the prosperity of the lineage, mathematics, wisdom, and the study of Vedanta philosophy. || 4 || **Jupiter** is the significator of eloquence, the king of mantras <note>sacred chants</note>, tantra, disciplined conduct, elephants, horses, vehicles, understanding of the Vedas, religious duties, the wealth of children, means of livelihood, the yoga of action, and the throne. || 5 || **Venus** is the significator of music, literature, service, the essence of wonder, passion, young women, amorous play, dalliance, diverse and colorful beauty, the power to enchant young women and kings, the science of 'Garuda' <note>charms against poison</note>, sorcery, the purity of garlands, great jewels, the eight forms of prosperity <note>the 'Ashta-Aishwarya' or supernatural powers</note>, poetry, the arts, equal enjoyment, and the spouse. || 6 || **Saturn** is the significator of greed, delusion, wickedness, the affliction of others, thunderbolts, cruelty, evil-mindedness, poverty, misfortune, disease, wind-related ailments <note>Vata disorders in Ayurvedic medicine</note>, deception, buffaloes, barley-gruel, black grains, longevity, and the means of survival. || 7 || **Rahu** is the significator of fame, prestige, and the royal umbrella <note>a symbol of high protection and status</note>. || 8 || Thus ends the 'Sarvartha Sutra'. ||

## ## Now Begins the Sarvarthachintamani

<note>The title *Sarvarthachintamani* translates to "The Gem that Fulfills All Purposes" or "The Wish-Fulfilling Gem of All Matters." It is a foundational 16th-century treatise on Hindu predictive astrology (Jyotisha) composed by Venkatesha Sharma.</note>

<note>The phrase "Now Begins" (original: *Atha*) is a traditional Sanskrit auspicious opening formula used to signal the commencement of a sacred or scientific text.</note>

<summary>This is the decorative title page for the Sarvarthachintamani, a significant classical Sanskrit text on Vedic astrology. It marks the formal opening of the treatise with traditional auspicious phrasing.</summary>
